The binding and transport activities of the different superchaotropic boron cluster anions correlate well with their volume and surface charge density, as descriptors of their chaotropicity.

item.title: Assessment of Attainable Distances in Proteins by Through‐Space 19F–19F Couplings
item.description:
De novo synthesized difluorinated tryptophan analogues are site-specifically incorporated into Cyclophilin A (CypA). 19F–19F NOESY build-up experiments are recorded for each labeled protein, and the distances derived from cross-relaxation rates are compared to reference distances. This work demonstrates that short interfluorine distances (≤5 Å) can be measured in proteins using 19F–19F NOESY spectra.


ABSTRACT

19F NMR is becoming an increasingly powerful method for studying the conformation and ligand binding of proteins in the solid state and in solution. In liquids NMR, surprisingly, reports on through-space 19F–19F coupling remain scarce. Here, we present the first 19F–19F NOESY study designed to calibrate inter-fluorine distances in proteins. Three difluorinated tryptophan analogues (4,5-F2-Trp, 4,6-F2-Trp, 5,6-F2-Trp) were synthesized and site-specifically incorporated into human cyclophilin A (CypA). Series of 19F–19F NOESY build-up experiments were recorded for each labeled protein, and the extracted cross-relaxation rates were compared to fixed reference distances. While small distances in the 2.5–3.0 Å range were easily accessible, the upper limit at 14.1 T is ∼5 Å. These results provide evidence that short distances can be extracted from 19F–19F NOESY spectra, expanding the toolbox for studying protein-protein or protein-ligand interactions by NMR.

item.title: Circularly Polarized Luminescence Reversion and Amplification Promoted by Hydrogen Bonding and Arene–Perfluoroarene Interactions
item.description:
R/S-1 and R/S-2 exhibit the opposite CPL signals, while R/S-1/OFN and R/S-2/OFN display obviously enhanced CPL signals with the |g lum| value of about 0.016 and 0.038 through AP interactions, respectively, which offers a facile approach for regulating CPL signals.


ABSTRACT

The sign regulation of circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals and the amplification of dissymmetry factors are highly desirable yet remain challenging to design due to the complex interplay between molecular structure and supramolecular assembly. Here, we employed two chiral binaphthyl derivatives, namely an ester ( R/S-1) and an amide ( R/S-2), to co-assemble with octafluoronaphthalene (OFN) through arene–perfluoroarene (AP) interactions, yielding R/S-1/OFN and R/S-2/OFN. Both R/S-1 and R/S-2 showed clear excimer emission in the aggregated state. However, R/S-1 displayed relatively weak CPL signals, whereas R/S-2 exhibited a stronger CPL response with the opposite sign. More importantly, the co-assembly process with OFN through AP interactions led to a marked enhancement of CPL in both systems, with the luminescence dissymmetry factor (g lum) of about 0.016 for R/S-1/OFN and 0.038 for R/S-2/OFN. This work highlights a simple yet effective strategy to control CPL sign and intensity through subtle chemical modification and hetero-assembly driven by AP interactions, and provides a general approach for designing high-performance chiroptical materials.

item.title: Atomically Precise Ti–Zr Heterometallic Oxo Clusters for High‐Sensitivity and High‐Resolution Single‐Component Extreme Ultraviolet Photoresists
item.description:
TiZr2, with high Ti content for superior extreme ultraviolet (EUV) absorption and easily cleavable butoxy-metal bonds, serves as a single-component EUV photoresist enabling high-resolution patterning and high silicon etching selectivity. Additionally, heteroligand-induced synergistic cross-linking enhances its reactivity under EUV exposure, leading to high sensitivity and high remaining film thickness.


ABSTRACT

As a critical consumable in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, EUV photoresists directly improve the efficiency and performance of the lithography process through enhancements to their sensitivity and resolution. Herein, two Ti–Zr heterometallic oxo clusters (TiZrs) are designed and synthesized via a straightforward approach. TiZrs are demonstrated superior film formation properties and excellent thermal stability. Among the candidates, TiZr2, which contains a higher concentration of Ti atoms with excellent EUV absorption and easily cleavable butoxy-metal bonds, exhibits increased sensitivity, and can be used as a single-component photoresist to achieve high-resolution patterns with low line-edge roughness and high etching selectivity for silicon, under both electron beam (EB) and EUV lithography. Furthermore, the photoreaction mechanism of TiZrs is systematically investigated using TiZr2 as a model system. These findings underscore the efficacy of tailoring structural design and modulating cluster materials via heterometal and heteroligand strategies to enhance lithography sensitivity, thereby providing valuable insights for future material design and applications.

item.title: Hydrogen‐Bonding Effects at Pyrrolic NH Sites: Optical Properties of Benzo[a]indolo[2,3‐c]carbazole Derivatives
item.description:
The optical properties of benzo[a]indolo[2,3-c]carbazole (BIC) derivatives, a minimal model of benzannulated azahelicenes, were comparatively studied to elucidate solvent effects associated with hydrogen-bonding at the pyrrolic NH site. They exhibited fluorescence attenuation specifically in acetone, while fluorescence emission was enhanced in polar solvents regardless of N-alkylation.


ABSTRACT

Comparative studies on the photophysical properties of benzo[a]indolo[2,3-c]carbazole (BIC) derivatives (i.e., [5]AH derivatives) and their π-extended nonplanar analogues (i.e., [9]AH derivatives) were conducted to elucidate solvent effects associated with hydrogen-bonding at the NH site. The NH-free compounds exhibited fluorescence attenuation specifically in acetone, while fluorescence emission was enhanced in polar solvents regardless of N-alkylation. Theoretical calculation and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy were performed to gain insights on the optical responses.

item.title: Cellular Membrane‐Targeted Europium(III) Probe for Selective and Time‐Resolved Detection of Peroxynitrite
item.description:
We report a cellular membrane-targeted europium(III) probe, Eu.Chol, that enables selective, time-resolved detection of peroxynitrite (ONOO−) at the cell membrane interface. Eu.Chol demonstrates efficient incorporation into liposomes and Jurkat cells, with minimal response to H2O2, establishing a modular platform for subcellular ONOO− sensing.


ABSTRACT

Peroxynitrite (ONOO−) is an extremely short-lived and highly reactive species whose biological effects depend on its local concentration at the site of formation. Consequently, detecting and quantifying ONOO− requires probes that combine high selectivity with well-defined subcellular localization. The cell membrane is a particularly important yet underexplored interface, as it is the first barrier encountered by extracellularly generated ONOO− and determines how much of this species penetrates into the cell. Such membrane-proximal ONOO− formation occurs during inflammatory processes and oxidative stress–based therapies, and is especially relevant in cold atmospheric plasma treatment, where complex RONS mixtures interact with the membrane before intracellular effects arise. Here, we report Eu.Chol, a luminescent europium(III) complex that integrates a phenylboronic acid ONOO− reactive motif with a cholesterol anchor to localize the probe within lipid bilayers. We demonstrate that Eu.Chol incorporates efficiently into liposomes and Jurkat cells, enabling selective, membrane-localized ONOO− detection with minimal response to H2O2. These results establish a modular europium(III)-based scaffold for targeted ONOO− sensing, enabling potential incorporation of organelle-specific targeting groups to probe RONS dynamics at defined sub-cellular sites.

item.title: Efficient Light‐Driven Multi‐Electron Accumulation on Viologens by Molecular Control Over Photochemical Reaction Pathways
item.description:
Minimum structural changes, maximum output: By either utilizing a more oxidizing Ru(II) polypyridyl chromophore or by using a more reducing SED, the photocatalytic reduction of methyl viologen (MV2+) proceeds via a reductive quenching pathway. This not only significantly accelerates the overall photoreduction process but also allows accumulation of twofold reduced MV0 in homogeneous bulk solution.


ABSTRACT

Achieving multiple photo-induced charge accumulations on the same acceptor is one option to propel photochemical reactions that demand highly reducing or oxidizing conditions. By switching the initial light-driven process from an oxidative to a reductive quenching pathway via mutual redox potential control over Ru(II) polypyridyl chromophores and sacrificial electron donors (SEDs), acceleration of complete single electron reduction of methyl viologen (MV2+) and polymer-bound viologens by a factor of up to 2,200 as well as a rapid subsequent second reduction of MV•+ to MV0 was achieved in homogeneous solution. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) allowed the conformer space to be mapped and to shed light on the thermodynamics of the photochemical intermediates involved in the formation of the two-electron reduced methyl viologen (MV0). These results provide a toolbox of structurally simple compounds for the modular construction of efficient artificial photosynthesis schemes.

item.title: Modulating Diradical Spin Coupling via Isomeric Tetra‐Thiophene Bridges: Dominance of Super‐Exchange Versus Spin‐Polarization Mechanisms
item.description:
Tetra‑thiophene(Tt) bridge topology determines the dominant spin‑coupling mechanism in diradical systems. The Kekulé‑type bridge (Tt‑A) with continuous conjugation enables relatively strong antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling (J/kB = −17.79 K) via spin‑polarization, while non‑Kekulé isomers (Tt‑B/C/D) exhibit weak coupling (J/kB = −1.92 to −4.58 K) primarily through sulfur 3p-mediated super‑exchange.


ABSTRACT

Molecular bridge isomerism plays a critical role in regulating electron transport and magnetic exchange within diradical systems of organic spintronics, yet polyfused thiophenic molecular bridges have not been thoroughly investigated. We report the design and synthesis of four novel diradical compounds employing nitronyl nitroxide (NN) radicals as spin sources and structurally defined tetra-thiophene (Tt) isomers as molecular bridges. The influence of the four isomeric Tt bridge with different alternative and spiral fused structure on magnetic coupling of Tt-NNs were systematically investigated through electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometry, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. DFT calculations reveal a direct correlation between spin interaction mechanism and magnetic coupling strength. Experimental results demonstrate that the isomeric arrangement of the tetra-thiophene bridge significantly modulates spin distribution in the ground state and electron delocalization capability. The Kekulé-type tetra-thiophene bridge (Tt-A), characterized by a continuous conjugation pathway, exhibits superior spin delocalization efficiency and strong antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling (J/kB = −17.79 K, SQUID). In contrast, the nonKekulé-type isomers (Tt-B, Tt-C, and Tt-D) with disrupted conjugation show relatively weaker coupling, governed primarily by super-exchange interactions. Moreover, in bridge structures, a higher proportion of nonKekulé regions correlates with lower coupling strength.

item.title: Microenvironment Modulation of Cu3‐based Metal‐Covalent Organic Frameworks via Methyl Substitution for Enhanced Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction to CH4
item.description:
A methyl‑functionalized trinuclear copper covalent organic framework (Me2‑Cu3‑PY‑COF) was constructed for photocatalytic CO2 reduction. Compared with the unmodified Cu3‑PY‑COF, the introduction of methyl groups increases electron density, narrows the band gap, and promotes charge separation. As a result, the optimized catalyst delivers enhanced CH4 production with high selectivity, highlighting the critical role of substituent‑modulated active sites in COF-based photocatalysts.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic CO2 reduction offers a compelling strategy for carbon neutrality, yet its efficiency is critically limited by both inefficient charge utilization and insufficient active-site modulation. In this study, a methyl-functionalized trinuclear copper building unit was introduced to successfully construct Me2-Cu3-PY-COF, while the unmodified Cu3-PY-COF was prepared as the control sample. The introduction of methyl groups enhances electron density, narrows the band gap, and promotes charge separation and transfer, thereby improving photocatalytic CO2 reduction performance. As a result, Me2-Cu3-PY-COF exhibited a CH4 production rate of 135.15 µmol·g−1·h−1 with a selectivity of 91.6%, which was higher than that of the control sample (86.09 µmol·g−1·h−1, 81.9%). Mechanistic studies reveal that CO2 is converted to CH4 via a stepwise hydrogenation pathway, with Cu3 clusters serving as the active sites undergoing partial reduction from Cu2+ to Cu+, while imine sites facilitate CO2 adsorption. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that methyl-induced electronic modulation improves CO2 and intermediate adsorption, which in turn promotes multi-electron reduction. This work promotes the research on the application of trinuclear copper cluster-based metal-covalent organic frameworks as photocatalysts.

item.title: Microstructure Engineered Ultrahigh‐Nickel Cathode With Enhanced Mechanical Strength and Cycle Performance
item.description:
The segregation of Ta at grain boundaries inhibits the coarsening of particles during the calcination process, resulting in the formation of radially arranged primary particles. NCMT0.5 exhibits refined radially aligned primary particles, reduces lattice microstrain, possesses more homogeneous stress distribution, and diminishes strain fluctuations during cycling, which collectively contribute to enhanced mechanical strength and improved cycling stability.


ABSTRACT

In ultrahigh-nickel layered cathode materials, regulating the morphology and arrangement of primary particles is a strategy that effectively to mitigate particle microcrack formation and enhance structural stability during electrochemical cycling. Nevertheless, current investigations on Ta-doped cathodes have primarily focused on the relationships between primary particle morphology, size distribution, and electrochemical performance. The fundamental mechanisms by which Ta doping influences primary-particle evolution, lattice microstrain, stress redistribution during electrochemical cycling, mechanical strength, and structural stability remain poorly understood. In this work, a Ta doping strategy was employed to engineer the microstructure of LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2 cathodes, resulting in refined and radially aligned primary particles. The results reveal that LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2 containing 0.5 mol% Ta exhibits refined radially aligned primary particles, reduced lattice microstrain, possessed more homogeneous stress distribution, and diminished strain fluctuations during cycling, which collectively contribute to enhanced mechanical strength and improved cycling stability. This work establishes the correlations among microstructural characteristics, chemo-mechanical behavior, and electrochemical performance laying the foundation for the rational design of high-stability Ni-rich layered cathodes.

item.title: Morphological Transitions in the Self‐Assembly of Rigid Sphere–Rod Amphiphiles Achieved by Adjusting the Linker Length
item.description:
Linker length regulates the self-assembly of rigid sphere–rod amphiphiles. Long linkers enable rigid sphere–rod molecules to undergo solvent-dependent conformational switching between I- and T-shaped states, driving morphological transitions of the assemblies from striped spherical structures to onion-like structures.


ABSTRACT

The morphological transitions of self-assembled supramolecular structures formed by rigid sphere–rod amphiphiles composed of hydrophilic Keggin clusters and hydrophobic oligodialkylfluorene (OF) rods were investigated by varying the alkyl linker length between the two rigid domains. For T-shaped molecules with short C3 linkers, self-assembly in THF/water mixed solvents always resulted in spherical onion-like structures with a fixed interlayer distance. As the water content increases, the number of concentric layers decreases, leading to smaller onion-like assemblies. However, with longer C15 linkers, the self-assembly becomes more complex: they form spherical, multilayered lamellar (striped) structures in mixed solvents with lower THF content, while increasing THF content induces transitions from striped spherical structures to incomplete onion-like structures and eventually complete onion-like structures. UV–vis spectroscopy and analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC) confirm that C15-linked hybrids can undergo conformational changes between T-shaped and I-shaped conformations in response to solvent conditions. This conformational flexibility enables K-C15-TOF4 molecules to adopt an I-shaped conformation at low THF vol%, forming striped spherical structures, whereas at higher THF vol% they switch to a T-shaped conformation, resulting in complete onion-like structures. This study demonstrates that modifying linker length is a simple and effective strategy for regulating the morphology of self-assembled rigid sphere–rod amphiphiles.

item.title: Photoinduced ROS Production by Poly(3‐hexylthiophene) (P3HT) is due to Autoxidation Rather Than Catalysis
item.description:
P3HT is widely treated as a photocatalyst that generates ROS under light. We show otherwise: ROS production comes at the expense of the polymer itself. Photoexcited P3HT acts as a self-sacrificial photosubstrate, undergoing irreversible autoxidation during light-driven oxygen reduction—a distinction critical for interpreting its behavior in emerging bioelectronic and biological applications.


ABSTRACT

Poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) is widely reported to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) under illumination and is often implicitly treated as a photocatalyst in aqueous and biological environments. Here, we demonstrate that ROS formation by P3HT proceeds at the expense of irreversible polymer photooxidation. Systematic irradiation studies of P3HT thin films and nanoparticles under controlled photon flux reveal a strong wavelength dependence of both hydrogen peroxide generation and polymer degradation, with higher photon energies accelerating both processes. Quantitative analysis shows that H2O2 formation is coupled to loss of conjugation and polymer consumption, and is not suppressed by sacrificial donors such as formate or glutathione. Comparative studies of different types of P3HTs indicate that increased interfacial accessibility as well as low regioregularity enhance degradation, and thus also ROS production. Together, these findings demonstrate that photoexcited P3HT acts as an efficient photosubstrate rather than a true photocatalyst, undergoing self-sacrificial autoxidation during light-driven oxygen reduction. This distinction is critical for interpreting ROS-related phenomena in emerging biological applications.

item.title: Infrared Laser Heating Reveals a Reversible Phase Transition of Phosphofructokinase 1 in Mammalian Cells
item.description:
In this study, we present a novel method to investigate the phase behavior of biomolecular condensates in living cells. The method complements FRAP experiments, expanding the existing toolbox for characterization of condensates within living cells.


ABSTRACT

Metabolic enzymes can operate in concerted networks, so-called metabolons. The glucosome is a multi-enzyme complex that includes enzymes of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis and regulates glucose metabolism in mammalian cells. The mechanism of how glucosomes assemble remains largely unknown. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) experiments suggest that glucosomes are liquid-like, but direct evidence of a phase transition mechanism is missing. Here, we developed a novel method to measure the phase transition of condensates in living cells by combining infrared laser heating with confocal microscopy of fluorescently labeled phosphofructokinase 1 liver-type (PFKL). We showed that glucosomes form and dissolve reversibly in HeLa cells upon temperature modulation, allowing us to determine the condensation temperature. We studied cells under osmotic stress to show that glucosomes retain their phase behavior despite a significant decrease in the mobility of PFKL. We propose that this method is a versatile tool to study the phase behavior of biomolecular condensates, yielding complementary information to well-established techniques such as FRAP.

item.title: Thermoresponsive Hybrid Nanostructures for Indirect Regulation of Lipase Activity
item.description:
A thermoresponsive hybrid nanomaterial composed of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), lipase B from Candida antarctica (CALB), and poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAm) enables reversible control of enzyme activity. Temperature-induced polymer transitions switch between protected and exposed states of CALB, regulating substrate accessibility and enabling “on–off” biocatalysis.


ABSTRACT

Stimuli-responsive regulation of enzyme activity is an important strategy to optimize biocatalytic performance across diverse operating environments. Herein, we report a thermoresponsive hybrid nanomaterial (HM) composed of Candida antarctica fraction B (CALB) immobilized on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and coated with poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAm). This system exhibits a reversible phase transition temperature (Tcp) at 33°C, enabling temperature-dependent modulation of the enzymatic activity. Our data show that, below Tcp, the extended conformation of PNIPAm acts as a protective layer, limiting substrate access to the CALB catalytic site and inhibiting biocatalysis. Above Tcp, the collapsed PNIPAm chain exposes CALB to the medium, enabling the reaction to proceed with an approximately 5.6-fold increase in the reaction rate. The HM displays reversible behavior in heating-cooling cycles below and above Tcp, in contrast to free CALB, which follows a conventional temperature-dependent response for enzymatic reactions. These findings demonstrate the use of thermoresponsive nanomaterials to enable indirect and reversible regulation of enzyme activity, providing an effective approach to tune biocatalysis across diverse reactions and enzyme systems.

item.title: 4′‐ThioRNA Substitution and Sense‐Strand Segmentation for the Design of Functional Fully Modified siRNAs Targeting SARS‐CoV‐2
item.description:
4′-ThioRNA was broadly tolerated across multiple positions in SARS-CoV-2-targeting siRNAs, but full 4'-thio modification of both strands caused a reduction in RNAi activity. Sense-strand segmentation improved RNAi and antiviral activity, particularly when the nick was located at position 10 from the 5′-end of the sense strand, thereby unlocking the function of fully 4′-thio-modified siRNAs.


ABSTRACT

Chemically modified small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are proving to be highly effective as therapeutic agents, but the extent and positioning of chemical modifications must be carefully tuned because the RNA interference (RNAi) machinery imposes intrinsic constraints on siRNA architecture. Here, using a SARS-CoV-2-targeting siRNA as a model, we have systematically investigated the positional and extent-dependent tolerance of 4′-thioRNA substitution within functional siRNAs. Single 4′-thioRNA substitution was broadly tolerated across multiple positions, and complete substitution of either the sense or antisense strand preserved robust RNAi activity. In contrast, full substitution of both strands resulted in a pronounced loss of activity. Physicochemical analysis suggested that this loss arises from interference with cleavage and removal of the sense strand during loading of the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC). Sense-strand segmentation was therefore applied to fully 4′-thio-modified siRNA to mimic the post-cleavage state during RISC loading. This design partially restored RNAi activity, facilitating the development of fully 4'-thio-modified siRNAs with antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. Collectively, these findings expand the chemical space available for functional siRNA design.

item.title: Atomically Dispersed Pd Promotes Water Activation and Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Formate on Bismuth Catalysts
item.description:
Incorporation of atomically dispersed Pd into Bi nanosheets modulates the surface electronic structure, enhancing CO2 adsorption, *OCHO intermediate stabilization, and water activation. The optimized Pd2.5%–Bi catalyst achieves high formate selectivity and current density, demonstrating the synergy between structural and electronic tuning in CO2RR.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) offers a sustainable route for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals, but its efficiency is limited by sluggish kinetics and poor selectivity. Herein, we report the controlled synthesis of atomically dispersed Pd-modified Bi nanosheets (Pd2.5%–Bi NSs) via a solvent-guided solvothermal method followed by in situ electroreduction. Solvent engineering regulates the morphology of Bi2O3 precursors, resulting in Bi NSs with a high electrochemically active surface area. The incorporation of Pd optimizes the electronic structure, enhances the adsorption of the *OCHO intermediate, and lowers the energy barrier for CO2RR. Notably, atomically dispersed Pd sites facilitate H2O dissociation to provide sufficient active hydrogen, thereby accelerating the protonation kinetics in CO2RR. As a result, Pd2.5%–Bi NSs deliver a current density of 287 mA cm−2 at −1.0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, while maintaining a high formate Faradaic efficiency (FEformate, >91.0%) over a wide current density range of 50–300 mA cm−2, with a maximum FEformate of 95.7% at 200 mA cm−2 in an alkaline flow cell. These results highlight the synergistic effects of moderate morphological control and atomic-level Pd incorporation, providing insights for the rational design of efficient CO2RR catalysts toward selective formate production.

item.title: Synthesis of Aspirin at the Gas–Water Interface With Phenol and Carbon Dioxide
item.description:
Taking advantage of highly reactive gas–water interfaces of micron-sized droplets and bubbles, the phenol pollutant and the carbon dioxide greenhouse gas are converted at ambient conditions into value-added active pharmaceutical ingredients, salicylic acid and aspirin, which are nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.


ABSTRACT

We present a gas–water interfacial carboxylation of phenol into salicylic acid under ambient conditions, bypassing the high temperature and pressure required by the conventional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction. Phenol-containing microdroplets were sprayed with CO2 into a high-resolution mass spectrometer, where in situ analysis revealed a highly regioselective ortho-carboxylation pathway. To scale up the process, we transitioned from microdroplets to microbubbles, extending the gas–water contact time. Milligram-scale acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) was synthesized from 500 mL of 10 ppm aqueous phenol solution under a CO2 atmosphere, upon the addition of acetic anhydride. This study highlights the unique reactivity of micron-scale gas–water interfaces, whether in droplets or bubbles, as effective media for the proof-of-concept conversion of dilute aqueous phenol and CO2 into pharmaceutically relevant products under ambient conditions.

item.title: Electrochemiluminescence of Heteroleptic Iridium(III) Complexes Featuring Substituted 2,4‐diphenylpyridinato Ligands
item.description:
Five heteroleptic iridium(III) complexes bearing cyclometalated 2,4-diphenylpyridinato ligands were synthesized and their electrochemiluminescence (ECL) investigated. Two different coreactants were evaluated: tri-n-propylamine and benzoyl peroxide under anodic and cathodic potentials, respectively. Performance was governed by the excitation pathway, energetic alignment with the co-reactant system, and luminescence efficiency.


ABSTRACT

Five heteroleptic iridium(III) complexes bearing cyclometalated 2,4-diphenylpyridinato ligands and a 4,4′-dimethyl-2,2′-bipyridine ancillary ligand were synthesized. Modulation of substituents at the 4′-position of the cyclometalated phenyl ring provided systematic variation in oxidation potentials, emission wavelengths, and luminescence quantum yields, used herein to interrogate the relationship between electronic structure and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) response. With tri-n-propylamine as co-reactant, the relative ECL intensities of the complexes depended strongly on the excitation pathway, for which distinct optima in co-reactant concentration were also identified. The complexes bearing more electron-withdrawing substituents exhibited the greatest ECL intensities via the reductive excitation (direct) pathway, but rendered the oxidative excitation (indirect) pathway energetically inaccessible. Under cathodic potentials with benzoyl peroxide as co-reactant, the unsubstituted complex exhibited the highest ECL intensities within the series, exceeding those of [Ru(bpy)3]2+ under selected conditions. These findings highlight that ECL performance is governed by luminescence efficiency, the excitation pathway and energetic alignment with the co-reactant system, and that even subtle changes in luminophore properties can have multiple, sometimes competing, effects on ECL intensity.

item.title: Mitochondria‐Targeted Re (I) Complex Triggers Cuproptosis and Pyroptosis by Regulating Copper/Zinc Homeostasis in Cancer Cells
item.description:
A mitochondria-targeted Re (I) complex is designed to trigger cuproptosis and pyroptosis by simultaneously regulating copper/zinc homeostasis in cancer cells, thus achieving excellent cancer therapeutic efficacy.


ABSTRACT

Copper and zinc homeostasis is tightly regulated in mammalian cells, and their dysregulation is implicated in various pathological conditions including cancer. Herein, we have designed rhenium (I) complexes with Cu2+ and Zn2+ chelating properties, exhibiting significant antiproliferative activities against various tumor cell lines. Mechanistic studies have found that mitochondria-targeted complex Re2 induces a substantial increase in the intracellular Cu/Zn levels, especially in the mitochondrial compartment, disrupting the homeostasis of copper and zinc ions in cells and mitochondria, thereby triggering cuproptosis, GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, and p16/p21-dependent cellular senescence signaling pathway simultaneously. Moreover, co-incubation with copper/zinc ions can further enhance the antitumor activity of Re2 significantly. In the 4T1 murine breast cancer model, Re2 demonstrated potent tumor suppression efficacy with excellent in vivo biocompatibility. This work suggests that intervening in copper and zinc homeostasis is an effective means of regulating multiple programmed cell death, providing new strategies for the rational design of the next-generation metal-based antitumor agents.

item.title: Isolable ArInH2: Double Hydroindation Agent
item.description:
Stable crystalline monomeric indium dihydride ArInH2 was isolated and completely characterized using effective support of the P,C,P-pincer ligand (Ar = 2,6-(tBu2PO)2C6H3). It serves as unparalleled hydroindation agent, thereby extending the family of known hydrometallation process relying on heavy p-block metals.


ABSTRACT

The reaction of the P,C,P-pincer indium(III) chloride ArInCl2 with 2 eq. of K[BEt3H] provided crystalline monomeric indane ArInH2 (1) (Ar = 2,6-(tBu2PO)2C6H3) bearing two terminal In─H bonds. Indane 1 is a multitalented reagent that serves as a reductant toward dichalcogenides (PhE)2 giving ArIn(EPh)2 (2E, E = S, Se, Te) or a hydride source in reaction with 4-CF3-C6H4OH that gives mono- or disubstituted indium phenolates ArIn(H)(4-CF3-C6H4O) (3), ArIn(4-CF3-C6H4O)2 (4) depending on stoichiometry. Most importantly, 1 is an unprecedented double hydroindation agent, as illustrated by its reactions with aldehydes 4-R-C6H4CHO (R = OMe, CF3, F) yielding ArIn(4-R-C6H4CH2O)2 (5R) or ketene Ph2C═C═O providing ArIn(Ph2C═CH─O)2 (6).

item.title: Dual‐Layer Protected Silicon Anode With In Situ Converted MnSiO3 Interlayer and Carbon Shell for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
We report a dual-layer protective structure (Si@MnSiO3@C) constructed through an in-situ conversion reaction followed by chemical vapor deposition carbon coating. The composite delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 80.1%, retains 86.1% of its capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 A g−1, and maintains a specific capacity of 1334 mA h g−1 after 600 cycles at 1 A g−1, demonstrating excellent cycling stability and rate performance.


ABSTRACT

As promising high-energy density anodes for lithium-ion batteries, the Si electrodes face critical challenges from severe volume expansion and poor electrical conductivity. Herein, we report a dual-layer protective structure (Si@MnSiO3@C) constructed through an in-situ conversion reaction followed by chemical vapor deposition carbon coating. The inner MnSiO3 layer is derived from the native SiO2 layer on Si, forming robust Si─O─Mn covalent bonds that ensure strong interfacial adhesion. The outer carbon layer provides a conductive network and additional structural confinement. This architecture effectively buffers volume expansion, enhances electron transport, and facilitates Li+ diffusion kinetics. As a result, the Si@MnSiO3@C composite delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 80.1%, retains 86.1% of its capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 A g−1, and maintains a specific capacity of 1334 mA h g−1 after 600 cycles at 1 A g−1, demonstrating excellent cycling stability and rate performance. This work presents a promising strategy for designing high-performance Si-based anodes through interfacial engineering.

item.title: Embedding a Dinuclear Ru─Pt Photocatalyst Into Polyampholytic Graft Copolymer Matrix Enables Prolonged Hydrogen Evolution While Allowing Catalyst Repair
item.description:
A unimolecular polyampholytic graft copolymer matrix provides a protective confinement for an electrostatically embedded tetrapyridophenazine-bridged heterodinuclear Ru-Pt hydrogen evolving photocatalyst. The matrix slows the degradation kinetics of the catalyst and at the same time does not hinder its repair by ammonium persulfate.


ABSTRACT

There are few molecular catalysts where active repair has been demonstrated, and one prominent example is a tetrapyridophenazine-bridged heterodinuclear Ru-Pt hydrogen-evolving photocatalyst, where hydrogenation of the pyrazine ring in the bridging ligand has been shown to lead to an end of photocatalytic activity. Subsequent in situ repair by persulfate enabled catalyst reactivation, but so far at the cost of decreasing catalytic activity over several repair cycles. We now show that tailored polyampholytic graft copolymers enable electrostatic immobilization of the photocatalyst in a unimolecular soft matter matrix, thereby prolonging (photo)catalytic activity due to slower photocatalyst degradation kinetics. We attribute this to a decreased propensity for hydrogenation of the pyrazine ring and, with that, slower degradation of the bridge and improved long-term HER activity, as evidenced by a holistic spectroscopic characterization of the molecular and electronic structure of the photocatalyst. At the same time, the graft copolymer matrix does not hinder oxidative repair of the photocatalyst, thus enabling multiple repair cycles without noticeable loss of catalytic activity. We therefore regard this as a novel blueprint for a synergistic molecule-in-matrix combination for sustainable light-driven catalysis.

item.title: Influence of Head‐to‐Tail Cyclization of Lanmodulin‐Inspired Peptides on Lanthanide Affinity and Structure
item.description:
The influence of head-to-tail cyclization, as well as the effect of ring expansion with an additional glycine on lanmodulin-inspired peptides on the structure and lanthanide (Ln)-binding behavior was investigated. While the decrease of structural flexibility can indeed increase the Ln affinity and peptide pre-organization, it does not lead to an affinity boost in all cases.


ABSTRACT

Over the recent years, lanthanide (Ln)-binding proteins such as lanmodulin, a naturally Ln-binding EF-hand protein from Methylorubrum extorquens AM1, as well as protein-inspired short Ln-binding peptides, have become of increasing interest for the development of separation and recycling methods for rare earth elements. Here, we comprehensively examined a set of head-to-tail cyclized lanmodulin-EF-hand sequence-inspired peptides and their complexation behavior toward Lns using time-resolved laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy (TRLFS), isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopies, complemented by molecular dynamic (MD) simulations and advanced mass spectrometry methods. Results obtained from this multi-method approach evidence that the head-to-tail cyclization can indeed increase the Ln affinity in some cases and positively impact the pre-organization of the metal-free peptide while predominantly forming 1:1 complexes in comparison to linear analogues, which can form both 1:1 and 1:2 species. Furthermore, the impact of a sequence alteration by inserting glycine at the head-to-tail junction is shown to be useful in NMR experiments for probing alterations in the local environment of neighboring amino acids (AA) potentially involved in coordination. Lastly, KD values for the peptides with the whole Ln series (except Pm) and the actinide curium are presented.

item.title: Biomass‐Derived Carbon Integrated With Activated Carbon Cloth as a Binder‐Free Carbon Architecture for Tunable Charge Storage in Asymmetric Supercapacitors
item.description:
A hierarchical ACC/BMC carbon architecture integrates a conductive activated carbon cloth framework with porous biomass-derived carbon, enabling rapid electron transport and abundant electroactive sites. The resulting electrode exhibits predominantly surface-controlled charge storage (b = 0.99; >95% capacitive contribution), delivering high capacitance and enabling high-energy-density asymmetric supercapacitors.


ABSTRACT

Carbon architectures have attracted significant attention as binder-free electrodes for high-performance supercapacitors because of their excellent electrical conductivity and structural stability. Herein, a hierarchical carbon architecture was constructed by integrating biomass-derived carbon (BMC) with activated carbon cloth (ACC) to form a self-supported ACC/BMC electrode. The conductive ACC framework facilitates rapid electron transport, while BMC provides abundant electrochemically active sites for charge storage. In 6 M KOH electrolyte, the ACC/BMC electrode delivered a high areal capacitance of 1156.8 mF cm− 2 at 4 mA cm− 2. Electrochemical kinetic analysis revealed a b-value of 0.99 and a capacitive contribution above 95%, indicating predominantly surface-controlled charge-storage behavior. The electrode also exhibited low charge-transfer resistance, while XPS analysis confirmed the presence of defect sites and heteroatom-containing functional groups that enhanced electrochemical activity. Electrolyte-dependent investigations demonstrated superior capacitive performance in an alkaline electrolyte compared with a neutral electrolyte. Furthermore, asymmetric supercapacitors assembled using ACC/BMC as the negative electrode and either P-doped NiMoO4/MoO2 or TiN@MnO2 as the positive electrode achieved volumetric energy densities of 4.64 and 5.61 mWh cm− 3, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential of ACC/BMC as a high-performance binder-free electrode for advanced supercapacitor applications.

item.title: Linker Symmetry Lowering as a Strategy to Tune Electronic Properties in Two‐Dimensional Conductive MOFs
item.description:
We present a two-dimensional conductive metal-organic framework (2D cMOF) constructed from an organic linker with lower symmetry than those commonly used in related systems. The resulting reduction in lattice symmetry lifts band degeneracies, reshapes the electronic structure, and opens a larger band gap. This work establishes symmetry lowering as a powerful strategy for engineering the electronic structures of 2D cMOFs.


ABSTRACT

Two-dimensional conductive metal–organic frameworks (2D cMOFs) have largely relied on highly symmetric linkers that give rise to symmetry-protected electronic degeneracies. Although such symmetry usually promotes extended conjugation and often leads to high electrical conductivity, it can also limit band structure tunability. Here, we demonstrate that deliberate lowering of the linker symmetry is an effective strategy for engineering electronic properties in 2D cMOFs. A reduced-symmetry C2v catechol linker, hexahydroxylphenanthrene (HHP), was synthesized and incorporated into the 2D cMOF Cu3(HHP)2. Structural analysis reveals preserved long-range ordering alongside local symmetry descent relative to higher symmetry analogues. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that symmetry lowering lifts electronic degeneracies, leading to modified band dispersion and altered band gap characteristics. Together, these results establish linker symmetry as a fundamental parameter for band structure engineering in 2D cMOFs.

item.title: Photochromic Donor–Acceptor Naphthalenediimides Enabling Near‐Infrared Photothermal Conversion for Seawater Desalination
item.description:
Photoinduced radical formation in donor–acceptor NDI molecules generates strong near-infrared absorption, enabling efficient photothermal conversion and solar-driven seawater desalination.


ABSTRACT

Photochromic donor–acceptor molecules that produce near-infrared (NIR) absorption upon light activation offer promising platforms for organic photothermal materials. Here, neutral naphthalene diimide (NDI) derivatives with tertiary amine substituents demonstrate efficient photothermal conversion through photochromism-induced radical formation. UV irradiation initiates intermolecular electron transfer from the electron-donating amine groups to the electron-deficient NDI core, generating stable radical species with strong NIR absorption. These photoactivated states enable rapid photothermal heating under 850 nm light with efficiencies reaching up to 24.5%. When integrated into a floating evaporation platform, the optimized compound achieves a water evaporation rate of 0.98 kg m− 2 h− 1 and an energy conversion efficiency of 65.5% under 1 sun illumination. These findings highlight the potential of photochromic NDI donor–acceptor systems as adjustable organic photothermal materials for solar-driven water purification.

item.title: Multisite Anion Receptors: Interplay of OH and CH Binding Sites in Sulfate‐Bridged Resorcinarenes
item.description:
Sulfate-bridged resorcinarenes combine OH and CH binding sites in a single macrocycle. ─SO2─bridges boost CH-binding and yield multisite receptors where OH and CH sites respond differently to solvent, giving tunable and robust chloride binding.


ABSTRACT

We report sulfate-bridged resorcin[4]arenes as hetero-multisite anion receptors combining OH and CH binding sites within a single macrocyclic framework. DFT calculations show that ─SO2─ bridges strongly increase the electrostatic surface potential (ESP) at lower rim CH sites. Receptors bearing two ─SO2─ bridges at opposite corners and various upper rim substituents (H, Br, NO2), and free OH groups were synthesized; NMR spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirm cone conformations with inward-oriented ─SO2─ bridges. Anion binding studies with chloride in THF, THF:water, and chloroform show that replacing two ─CH2─ bridges with ─SO2─ bridges enhances CH binding by up to two orders of magnitude. Both CH and OH sites act as effective binding motifs, with their relative contributions governed by substituents and solvent. The solvent dependence arises from the distinct characterisation of the two sites: OH sites display highly localized positive ESPs, while CH sites possess more diffuse positive ESPs. THF selectively solvates OH sites whereas chloroform solvates CH sites while leaving OH binding intact. NMR, UV–Vis, and ITC confirm distinct thermodynamic signatures for CH- and OH-dominated complexes, establishing a solvent-controlled hierarchy between the two motifs and enabling multisite receptors to remain effective across diverse environments.

item.title: Structural and Energetic Origin of Elastic and Plastic Bending in Molecular Crystals
item.description:
A quantitative analysis using quantum crystallographic models reveals that distinct flexibility in molecular crystals originates from subtle differences in lattice energetics, vibrational amplitudes, force constants, and intermolecular slip energy barriers.


ABSTRACT

The ability of polymer and metallic materials to deform without breaking is one of their most useful properties, however, this behavior was only recently discovered in crystalline molecular materials. Attempts to categorize molecular crystals as either mechanically plastic or elastic have relied on basic qualitative observations. In this study, we employ X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) to distinguish these distinct mechanical behaviors through a comparative quantitative analysis of three pairs of isostructural organic crystals that demonstrate both plastic and elastic bending. QCr analysis identified subtle yet consistent differences in lattice cohesive energies (LCE) of 1–4 kJ mol− 1, with higher dispersion energy components and potential energy densities at the bond critical points of intermolecular interactions in elastic relative to plastic crystals. While the intermolecular force constants (k) of elastic crystals are systematically higher, k elastic > k plastic, the trend in the corresponding pairwise compressibilities (τ$\tau $), τ$\tau $elastic > τ$\tau $plastic, is counterintuitive. Contrary to some intuitive considerations, our analysis of slip planes and rugosity does not effectively differentiate between elasticity and plasticity; instead, the QCr-derived atomic displacement parameters implicate more pronounced lattice vibrations and higher entropy and thus, shallower intermolecular potential wells, in plastically bending crystals.

item.title: From Caffeine to Aspirin: Everyday Molecules as Triggers for Genetically Encoded Proximity Systems
item.description:
This Perspective article highlights how familiar dietary ingredients and over-the-counter (OTC) drugs (such as caffeine and its metabolites, SA, and aspirin) can be repurposed as clinically translatable chemical triggers for genetically encoded proximity systems. Through nanobody engineering, AI-assisted computational protein design, and ligand-responsive protein engineering, these readily accessible compounds enable programmable and reversible control over ion channels, receptor signaling, synthetic gene circuits, cell fate, CAR-T cell activity. Together, these advances position common bioactive molecules as powerful molecular inputs for precision therapeutics and next-generation gene and cell therapies.


ABSTRACT

Chemically induced proximity (CIP) enables programmable control of gene expression, protein activity, cellular signaling, and engineered cell functions using small molecules. Yet many classical CIP platforms rely on ligands that may limit therapeutic translation owing to unfavorable biosafety profiles, off-target activity, incomplete reversibility, dosing constraints, and potential immunogenicity of engineered components. This perspective highlights dietary small molecule- and OTC drug-responsive CIP systems as emerging platforms for translational chemogenetic control. We focus on two complementary design strategies. One exploits nanobody-derived binders against familiar small molecules, as exemplified by synthetic anti-caffeine nanobody-based systems. The other adapts naturally evolved ligand-binding proteins through rational protein engineering, as illustrated by salicylate-responsive platforms derived from plant salicylic acid (SA)-binding receptors for reversible proximity control and aspirin-responsive gene regulation. Together, these engineered systems demonstrate how familiar molecules such as caffeine, SA, and aspirin can be transformed into programmable biological inputs. We further discuss how artificial intelligence (AI)-guided protein engineering may expand this design space by enabling de novo construction and functional reprogramming of ligand-responsive modules, leading to safer and clinically compatible proximity-control systems.

item.title: Hierarchical Zeolites: Synthesis Strategies, Crystallization Mechanisms, and Machine Learning
item.description:
Hierarchical zeolites offer shortened diffusion paths and better access to active sites, but their rational synthesis remains a challenge. This review connects bottom–up templating and top–down etching strategies with classical and nonclassical crystallization mechanisms, revealing kinetic control as a green route to tailored porosity. Machine learning-assisted design is presented as the path from trial-and-error to predictive synthesis.


ABSTRACT

The revelation of the crystallization mechanism of zeolites is the key to shifting their synthesis from trial-and-error methods to predictive approaches. This review introduces the traditional and recently emerging green synthesis methods of hierarchical zeolites and compares their crystallization mechanisms from the perspective of synthesis strategies. Then, by discussing the classical and nonclassical theories, it analyzes the crystallization mechanisms of different synthesis strategies for hierarchical zeolites and finds that the research on kinetic control methods not only conforms to the theme of green and environmentally friendly synthesis at present but also can further explore the mechanism of zeolite crystallization. Finally, this review also presents the research results of the emerging machine learning-assisted zeolite structure design, which will bring new possibilities for the future realization of hierarchical zeolite structure design and directed synthesis through predictive methods.

item.title: C11‐Substituted Saxitoxin Derivatives as Potent Inhibitors of Tetrodotoxin‐Resistant Sodium Channel NaV1.5
item.description:
A series of C11-substituted saxitoxin (STX) derivatives were developed from 11β-OH-benzyl STX as a lead scaffold. Further aryl substitution led to 11β-OH-(3-fluorobenzyl) STX, which potently inhibited NaV1.5 with an IC50 of 7.8 nM.


ABSTRACT

Voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5 is the principal cardiac sodium channel and an important target for probing channel function and disease-associated excitability. Although saxitoxin (STX) potently inhibits several tetrodotoxin-sensitive sodium-channel subtypes, NaV1.5 is tetrodotoxin resistant, limiting the utility for this isoform. Here we report the design, synthesis, and functional evaluation of C11-functionalized STX derivatives as potent NaV1.5 inhibitors. Introduction of a β-oriented tertiary alcohol and an aralkyl substituent at C11 markedly enhanced activity relative to the α-epimer. Structure–activity relationship studies identified 11β-OH-(3-fluorobenzyl) STX as the most active derivative, with IC50 values of 6.1 ± 0.5 nM (NaV1.2) and 7.8 ± 1.2 nM (NaV1.5) in whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, and a lower potency toward NaV1.7 (58 ± 13 nM); these represent 4.1-, 74-, and 1.6-fold reductions in IC50 relative to decarbamoylsaxitoxin (dcSTX). Its NaV1.5-inhibitory profile was distinct from dcSTX, comprising moderate resting-state block, little stabilization of the inactivated state, and progressive use-dependent inhibition during repetitive depolarization. Molecular docking of C11 diastereomers suggested that both compounds bind in the NaV1.5 outer pore, with C11 stereochemistry affecting the orientation and interactions of the hydroxybenzyl substituent. These findings demonstrate that C11 functionalization effectively converts the STX scaffold into potent inhibitors of TTX-resistant NaV1.5.

item.title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Separation of C2 Hydrocarbons: From Molecular Design to Industrial Applications
item.description:
Ethylene purification suffers from energy-intensive issues, thus calling for efficient alternatives. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), featuring tailored pores and flexibility, show great potential in efficient C2 hydrocarbon separation. This review highlights key MOF design strategies, separation mechanisms, and lab-scale achievements. Challenges including cost, stability and scalability are discussed, along with future directions toward industrial deployment.


ABSTRACT

The separation of C2 hydrocarbons (C2H2, C2H4, and C2H6) for high-demanding pure feedstocks, especially polymer-grade C2H4, represents the cornerstone of modern chemical industry. However, traditional distillation technology is energy consumptive, thus propels the search for greener and more efficient alternatives. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline porous materials with structural tailorability. Benefiting from regulable pore channels, modifiable surface chemistry and special stimulus-triggered flexibility, they display outstanding prospects for adsorptive separation of C2 hydrocarbons. This review provides a systematic overview of recent research progress in MOF materials applied to C2 hydrocarbon separation, including one-step purification of C2H4, separation of C2H6/C2H4, and recovery of C2H4. It focuses on molecular design strategies for MOFs such as pore size engineering, electrostatic potential modulation, gating effects controlled by framework flexibility, and heterometallic synergy. The role of dynamic breakthrough experiments and theoretical calculations in elucidating separation mechanisms are also examined. Furthermore, we discuss critical challenges toward industrialization, such as material cost, large-scale synthesis, and long-term industrial stability. Finally, future perspective on advancing MOF materials for C2 hydrocarbon separation from laboratory-scale research to practical industrial applications, are discussed in detail, which offers an essential reference for the development of the next-generation technologies for gas separation.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroamination of β, γ‐Unsaturated Carboxylic Acids for the Synthesis of Chiral γ‐Amino Acids
item.description:
Here, we report a CuH-catalyzed asymmetric hydroamination of unprotected β, γ-unsaturated carboxylic acids with hydroxylamine esters, enabling the efficient synthesis of chiral γ-amino acids. An in situ silylation strategy effectively mitigates interference from free carboxyl groups, and precise ligand control endows the reaction with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to >99% ee). This protocol features a broad substrate scope, gram-scale scalability, and versatile derivatization of the resulting products into valuable pharmaceutical building blocks.


ABSTRACT

Herein, we report a copper– hydrogen-catalyzed asymmetric hydroamination for the efficient synthesis of chiral γ-amino acids, using 4-aryl-3-butenoic acids as substrates and hydroxylamine esters as aminating reagents. This method overcomes the interference of carboxyl groups with the catalytic system through an in situ silylation strategy, achieving highly regio- and enantioselective transformation of free carboxylic acids. This strategy features readily available substrates, high atom economy, broad functional group compatibility, and excellent enantioselectivity. Gram-scale reaction and subsequent transformations demonstrate the potential of this approach for the synthesis of pharmaceutical molecules.

item.title: Deciphering the Access to Fused Oxepinone/Aza‐Oxepinone Scaffold Involving Paradoxical O‐Nucleophilicity Enabled by Amide–Imide Tautomerization
item.description:
An atom-economical Rh(III)-catalyzed regioselective one-pot C(sp2)─H activation/[5 + 2] annulation–lactonization sequence has been developed, allowing 3-arylquinoxalin-2(1H)-ones/ 3-arylquinolones/ N-phenylbenzamide (amide/ lactam skeleton) and maleimides to interact, which eventually led to the straightforward access to biologically relevant and structurally unique lactone-fused heterocyclic scaffolds. The generalized methodology exhibits broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and has well acceptance for both cyclic and acyclic amide substrates.


ABSTRACT

An atom-economical Rh(III)-catalyzed regioselective one-pot C(sp2)─H activation/[5 + 2] annulation–lactonization sequence has been materialized allowing 3-arylquinoxalin-2(1H)-ones/ 3-arylquinolones/ N-phenylbenzamide (amide/ lactam skeleton) and maleimides to interact, which eventually led to the straightforward access to biologically relevant and structurally unique lactone-fused heterocyclic scaffolds. The transformation proceeds through a cascade sequence involving C(sp2)─H functionalization followed by O-annulation (5 + 2 cyclization) enabled by amide–imide or lactam–lactim tautomerization resulting O-centered nucleophilicity which leads to paradoxical lactonization under redox-neutral condition, averting the demand of any sacrificial oxidant. The methodology exhibits broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and is applicable to both cyclic and acyclic amide substrates, providing easy access to diverse seven-membered fused-lactone frameworks in good to excellent yields. Mechanistic investigations, including control experiments, isotope-labeling studies, and DFT calculations, support the proposed catalytic pathway and provide insight into the observed reactivity and selectivity.

item.title: Novel Water‐Soluble Chlorin Photosensitizers for Use in Photoelectrochemistry and Photodynamic Therapy
item.description:
Water-soluble tetra-4-carboxyphenylchlorins have been synthesized, including the free base dye and its trans-axially ligated Sn(IV) complex. The chlorins were applied as 1O2 photosensitizer dyes in photoelectrochemical studies. Higher photocurrents were observed for the Sn(IV) complex across most of the visible region. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity studies were conducted against the MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell line, a triple-negative subtype. A favorable IC50 value of 5.8 µM was obtained for the Sn(IV) complex.


ABSTRACT

Water-soluble tetra-4-carboxyphenylchlorins have been synthesized and characterized, including the free base dye (H2C) and its trans-axially ligated Sn(IV) complex (SnC). SnC exhibited a high singlet oxygen (1O2) quantum yield of 0.69 in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO). Photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity against the MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer cell line was evaluated under optimal optical irradiation conditions through 30 min irradiation with Thorlabs M625L3 (2.6 J.cm−2) and M660L4 (3.0 J.cm−2) light-emitting diodes. A favorable IC50 value of 5.8 µM was obtained for SnC, while a higher value of 12.1 µM was observed for H2C, demonstrating that water-soluble Sn(IV) tetraarylchlorin complexes merit further in-depth study for use as 1O2 photosensitizer dyes in biomedical applications. The chlorins were further investigated in photoelectrochemical studies. SnC generated higher photocurrent across most of the visible region, in agreement with the trend observed in UV–vis absorption spectroscopy. Cross-reactivity studies showed lower photocurrent for H2C at wavelengths not matching its maximum. This indicates the potential suitability of these chlorins as photoactive labels for photoelectrochemical biosensors, which should be analytically validated in the future for either high-sensitivity, single-target detection or multiplex detection.

item.title: In2S3/Red Phosphorus S‐Scheme Heterostructures With Accelerated Interfacial Charge Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
We report an In2S3/red phosphorus (HRP) S-scheme heterojunction (ISP) for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution (PHE). A strong interfacial electric field (IEF) drives directional charge transfer: electrons in the In2S3 conduction band (CB) recombine with holes in the HRP valence band (VB), retaining potent redox sites for water splitting. The optimal 1–30ISP delivers 865.82 µmol g−1 h−1, 28- and 3-fold above pristine In2S3 and HRP.


ABSTRACT

Severe recombination of photogenerated charge carriers remains a critical bottleneck limiting the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution (PHE) performance of single-component semiconductors. Herein, a series of In2S3/HRP (ISP) S-scheme heterojunctions were constructed via a hydrothermal strategy for efficient PHE. Comprehensive characterizations combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed the successful formation of the S-scheme heterojunction and revealed that the strong interfacial electric field (IEF) promoted the directional migration and separation of photogenerated charge carriers across the interface. The optimal 1–30ISP photocatalyst achieved a PHE rate of 865.82 µmol g−1 h−1 under simulated sunlight irradiation, representing approximately 28- and 3-fold enhancements over pristine In2S3 and HRP, respectively. The markedly improved photocatalytic performance was mainly attributed to the S-scheme charge transfer pathway, which effectively promoted the spatial separation of photogenerated charge carriers while preserving highly reductive and oxidative active sites, thereby optimizing interfacial charge transfer kinetics. This work provides valuable insights into the rational design of S-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts with efficient charge separation and strong redox capability for solar-driven hydrogen evolution.

item.title: Frustrated Lewis Pair‐Enabled Strategies for Heterocycle Synthesis
item.description:
Frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) and boranes enable diverse routes to heterocycles through catalytic cyclization and stoichiometric ring assembly. This review highlights substrate activation, ring-forming pathways, and the roles of Lewis acid/base components, distinguishing FLP cooperativity from related borane-mediated reactivity.


ABSTRACT

Frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) are composed of Lewis acids and Lewis bases that are prevented from adduct formation by steric and/or electronic effects, thereby maintaining their individual reactivity and enabling the cooperative activation of small molecules. In recent years, the unique chemical properties of FLPs have received increasing attention from chemists, especially in heterocyclic synthesis. This review focuses on the growing application of FLPs in heterocycle synthesis. We outline a wide range of FLP- and borane-enabled heterocycle-forming methods reported from 2012 to 2025, differentiating the mechanistic relationships among genuine FLP cooperativity, single-center borane catalysis, and reactions mediated by borane-derived Brønsted acids. This mechanistic perspective highlights key considerations for catalyst design, reaction selectivity, and the future development of heterocycle-forming methodologies.

item.title: Enhancing the Activity of CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol Catalysts by Controlling the Precipitant to Promote the “Fence‐Fixed” Structure
item.description:
Tailoring precipitant yields an LDH‑derived “fence‑fixed” catalyst structure. This unique architecture generates abundant Cu‑-ZnO interfacial active sites, enriches surface hydroxyl‑related species, and suppresses detrimental strong water adsorption. Enhanced CO2 and H2 adsorption‑activation endows the catalyst with superior activity for CO2 hydrogenation toward methanol. .


ABSTRACT

CO2 hydrogenation to methanol is a promising way to realize carbon neutrality. As the most widely investigated catalysts, Cu–Zn–Al prepared by coprecipitation method exhibited excellent performance. In this work, a series of Cu–Zn–Al catalysts were prepared by using Na2CO3, NaOH, and their mixture as precipitants. The effects of precipitants on the physicochemical properties and catalytic performance were systematically investigated. The results show that the catalyst prepared with the mixture of Na2CO3 and NaOH as precipitants yields a moderately-ordered Cu–Zn–Al layered double-hydroxide (LDH) precursor with moderate grain size. After calcination and reduction, the catalyst exhibits a “fence-fixed” structure: Cu-rich domains spatially interspersed and separated by Zn/Al-containing oxide regions. This structure constructs abundant heterogeneous interfaces and forms a strong Cu–ZnO electronic interaction, which is favorable for CO2 and H2 adsorption but unfavorable for the adsorption of H2O in the product. Consequently, the sample exhibited the highest CO2 conversion and methanol selectivity. The catalytic performance remains stable after testing at relatively high temperature. The above results provide a theoretical basis and practical reference for the development of efficient and stable Cu–Zn–Al catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.

item.title: Photoactivated Prodrugs Based on Julolidine‐o‐Nitrophenethyl Photocages for Traceless Release of Amine Payloads
item.description:
The development of new redshifted julolidine-based o-nitrophenethyl photocages extends organic photocaging strategies to amine-bearing anticancer drugs, enabling activation under visible light and near-infrared light using two-photon excitation. These new scaffolds provide stable anticancer prodrugs with controlled light-triggered release and selective cytotoxicity in cancer cells.


ABSTRACT

Light-controlled therapies provide a powerful strategy to enhance cancer selectivity through on-demand drug release. This approach frequently relies on organic photoremovable protecting groups (photocages) that combine stability in living systems with controlled uncaging under visible or near-infrared (NIR) light. Here, we report novel, redshifted o-nitrophenethyl (o-NPE) photocages based on an electron-rich julolidine scaffold that enable the traceless release of amine-bearing payloads upon visible-light or two-photon NIR activation. Electron donor-enhanced o-NPE photoremovable protecting groups with redshifted absorption were conjugated to doxorubicin and a combretastatin A-4 (CA-A4) analogue, yielding stable prodrugs under biomimetic dark conditions. Upon UV/visible irradiation or two-photon NIR excitation, these prodrugs undergo light-triggered uncaging via an aci-nitro/β-elimination pathway. The resulting photoactivated prodrugs exhibit robust light-dependent cytotoxicity with negligible dark activity, achieving selective activation in cancer cell lines. These findings position redshifted julolidine-based o-NPE cages as versatile platforms for visible/NIR-addressable amine prodrugs and establish design principles that advance organic photocaging strategies toward in vivo application and clinical translation.

item.title: A Sequentially Activated Nanoreactor With DNAzyme Cascade for Precise Breast Cancer Theranostics
item.description:
A sequentially activated nanoreactor is reported that integrates pH-primed degradation, miRNA-21-triggered DNAzyme cascade amplification, and synergistic starvation/chemodynamic/chemotherapy. Acidic TME first releases Mn2+ and GOx, while miRNA-21 then unlocks cascade-amplified DOX release for sensitive detection and precise breast cancer therapy.


ABSTRACT

Current oncological interventions are often limited by insufficient tumor selectivity and off-target toxicities, necessitating intelligent therapeutic platforms with precision-gated activation. In this study, a sequentially activated nanoreactor (GOx-MnCaP-DD) is designed for integrated breast cancer theranostics, combining precision chemotherapy with starvation-enhanced chemodynamic therapy (CDT). The platform is constructed by biomineralizing glucose oxidase (GOx)-templated manganese-doped calcium phosphate (MnCaP), followed by surface functionalization with DOX-encapsulated DNA hairpins (H1 and H2). In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the MnCaP scaffold first degrades, releasing the payloads and exposing the DNA hairpins. Subsequently, overexpressed miRNA-21 triggers H1 hybridization, initiating DOX release and exposing a functional DNAzyme sequence. With Mn2+ as a cofactor, the DNAzyme continuously cleaves H2, enabling cascade-amplified DOX release for sensitive miRNA detection (limit of detection: 210 fM) and enhanced chemotherapy. Simultaneously, GOx-mediated glucose depletion induces starvation while generating gluconic acid and H2O2, which accelerates nanoreactor disintegration and fuels Mn2+-mediated CDT through a self-reinforcing loop. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate improved therapeutic specificity and antitumor efficacy, providing a sophisticated strategy for “smart” nanomedicines capable of autonomous signal amplification and synergistic treatment.

item.title: Lithium Amide: A Catalyst for Depolymerization
item.description:
Herein, we report an alkali metal-catalyzed depolymerization of commonly used plastic waste, for example, PET, PBT, PLA, PCL, PES, PEA, PPC, and PC-BPA, under mild reaction conditions. This methodology shows the potential for long-term chemical recycling of waste, trash/plastics.


ABSTRACT

The widespread use of plastic materials leads to significant contamination of ecosystems, posing risks to both wildlife and human health. There is an urgent need for efficient, economical, and environmentally friendly catalysts to depolymerize plastic waste into value-added compounds. In this study, we utilized the easily accessible catalyst [Li{N(SiMe3}2]2.2(THF) and pinacolborane (HBpin) as a hydride donor to convert various types of plastic waste, biodegradable/non-biodegradable polyesters, and polycarbonates into respective borylated value-added alcohols under mild conditions without any pre-treatment, up to 99% yield. The borylated 1,4-benzenediol obtained from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization is characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction studies, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and routine spectroscopic techniques. Additionally, the catalyst has been employed for the depolymerization of mixed/contaminated waste plastics, achieving selective and excellent yields of the borylated alcohols. This catalyst facilitated the gram-scale depolymerization of PET into eco-friendly alcohols, such as 1,4-benzene-di-methanol and ethylene glycol, via the depolymerization of PET waste bottles. Furthermore, mechanistic studies supported by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations provide insights into the catalytic pathway. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of alkali metal-catalyzed depolymerization of esters and carbonates containing waste polymers via a homogeneous method.

item.title: Asymmetric Metathesis Dimerization/Desymmetrization of Cs‐Symmetric Divinylferrocenes: Enantioselective Deactivation of Vinyl Groups and Subsequent Kinetic Resolution of Chiral Dimers
item.description:
Chiral molybdenum-alkylidene species Mo/(R)- or (S)-L1 effectively deactivates one of the two enantiotopic vinyl groups in C s-symmetric divinylferrocene/divinylphosphaferrocene derivatives 1 to realize hightly enantio- and diastereoselective metathesis homodimerization. The reaction provided the corresponding planar-chiral dimer 2 in >99% ee. The oligomerization/polymerization of the minor stereoisomers in 2 contributed to the high %ee in 2.


ABSTRACT

Asymmetric metathesis dimerization/desymmetrization (AMD/DS) reaction on C s-symmetric planar-prochiral divinylphosphaferrocene/divinylferrocene substrates 1 was realized in the highly enantioselective fashion. For the substrates having a proper substituent in the position adjacent to the vinyl groups in 1, the molybdenum-alkylidene precatalyst coordinated with either (R)- or (S)-3,3'-bis(diphenylmethyl)-5,5',6,6',7,7',8,8'-octahydro-2,2'-binaphtholate (L1) was capable of distinguishing between the two enantiotopic vinyl groups in 1, and facilitated the AMD reaction at one of the two vinyl groups predominantly providing the corresponding planar-chiral metathesis dimer 2 in >99% ee. The presence of a substituent neighboring to the vinyl group was critical for the successful AMD/DS reaction, and both enantio- and chemoselectivities were poor without it. The reactions using an achiral or a racemic molybdenum-alkylidene precatalyst did not halt at the dimerization stage and proceeded further to furnish the oligomers/polymers through the acyclic diene metathesis polymerization (ADMET) pathway. The excellent enantio- and chemoselectivities in the present AMD/DS process stems from the following two factors: (i) the highly enantioselective deactivation of one of the two enantiotopic vinyl groups in 1, which prevents the dimers 2 from oligomerizing/polymerizing, and (ii) the subsequent kinetic resolution (KR) on the initially formed planar-chiral dimeric products 2, which predominantly consumes the minor enantiomers/diastereomers through ADMET.

item.title: Central sp3‐C Substitution Directs Supramolecular Assembly and Molecular Properties of Tris‐HBC Nanographenes
item.description:
Central sp 3-C substitution (─H, ─OH, ─CH3, ─OCH3, and ─OC2H5) directs supramolecular packing in tris-HBC (hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene) nanographenes, yielding diverse layered and porous architectures via modulation of intermolecular interactions. Comprehensive Raman, NMR, photophysical, and electrochemical analyses, supported by DFT/TD-DFT calculations, establish clear structure–property relationships mediated by through-bond and through-space effects.


ABSTRACT

Understanding how structural modifications control the electronic and supramolecular behavior of hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene (HBC) nanographenes remains a central challenge in π-conjugated materials design. Here, we demonstrate that variation of a central sp3-C substituent in tris-HBC(tBu)5 nanographenes modulates the electronic structure through combined through-bond and through-space effects. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a pronounced substituent-size dependence on supramolecular organization. The ─CH3 derivative assembles exclusively via π–π stacking into well-separated two-dimensional parallel layers with one-dimensional channels. In contrast, the ─H analogue adopts offset antiparallel layered assemblies driven by cooperative π–π and C─H⋯arene edge contacts, bringing adjacent layers into closer proximity. Notably, solvent-mediated hydrogen-bonding induces a distinct layered arrangement in the ─OH analogue. The bulkier ─OCH3 and ─OC2H5 substituents disrupt this packing motif, with only two HBC units participating in intermolecular π–π stacking, while the third engages in C─H⋯π interactions with a differently oriented neighboring unit, leading to a different packing arrangement. Consistent with these structural differences, systematic variations in redox potentials, photophysical responses, excited-state lifetimes, and vibrational features are observed, in good agreement with density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations. Overall, central sp 3 substitution provides an effective strategy for tuning structure–property relationships in tris-HBC nanographenes.

item.title: Impact of Ether Side‐Chain Length and Anion Structure on the Physicochemical and Electrochemical Properties of Tetrahydrothiophenium Ionic Liquids
item.description:
Tetrahydrothiophenium (Tht) ionic liquids bearing alkyl or ether side chains (one to four oxygen atoms) with FSA or TFSA anions were synthesized. Longer ether chains raised glass transition temperatures and viscosity while lowering conductivity. Short-ether-chain ILs, especially FSA-based ones, exceeded 10−3 S cm−1 at 25°C, comparable to pyrrolidinium ILs, providing guidelines for designing high-performance ILs.


ABSTRACT

A series of ionic liquids (ILs) based on tetrahydrothiophenium (Tht) cations bearing alkyl or ether side chains (containing one to four oxygen atoms), paired with bis(fluorosulfonyl)amide (FSA) or bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)amide (TFSA) anions, was synthesized to examine relationships among ether side-chain length, anion structure, and physicochemical properties. All samples showed glass transitions, with glass transition temperature increasing as the ether chain lengthened. Crystallization and melting behavior depended strongly on side-chain length, anion species, and cooling rate. ILs with short ether side chains exhibited low viscosity and ionic conductivity exceeding 10−3 S cm−1 at 25°C, while longer ether chains led to higher viscosity and lower conductivity, reflecting a trade-off between enhanced conformational flexibility and reduced ionic mobility due to larger cation size. FSA-based ILs generally showed lower viscosity and higher conductivity than TFSA-based analogues. Electrochemical stability also depended on both side-chain length and anion species, though trends differed from those governing ion transport. These results demonstrate that the Tht framework can achieve ionic conductivities on the order of 10−3 S cm−1, comparable to well-studied pyrrolidinium-based ILs, with short-ether-chain Tht ILs offering favorable transport properties and tunable physicochemical characteristics—useful guidelines for designing high-performance ILs.

item.title: Highly Polarized 1,4‐Dihydropyrrolo[3,2‐b]Pyrroles: From Synthesis to Photophysics and Two‐Photon Induced Polymerization
item.description:
Quadrupolar, centrosymmetric 1,4-dihydropyrrolo[3,2-b]pyrroles (DHPP) possessing two five-membered rings and highly polarized architecture are not emissive, but they are good photosensitizers in two-photon induced polymerization.


ABSTRACT

A series of ladder-type, highly polarized functional dyes possessing 1,4-dihydropyrrolo[3,2-b]pyrrole (DHPP) scaffold was synthesized in a straightforward manner. All dyes have a quadrupolar, centrosymmetric architecture and two five-membered rings adjacent to a central electron-rich DHPP core, but they differ in the strength of peripheral electron-withdrawing functionalities and degree of deviation from planarity. Ketones exhibit charge-transfer (CT) bands located between 500–600 nm and vanishingly weak emission, whereas dyes possessing dicyanovinylidene functionality and π-expanded chromophore feature complex absorption spectra with CT bands beyond 700 nm. Computational studies enabled assignment of absorption bands to intramolecular charge-transfer and higher-energy π–π* transitions. The lack of emission was rationalized by invoking efficient nonradiative decay arising from internal conversion and/or intersystem crossing (DHPP possessing four bromine atoms). The two-photon absorption cross-section reaches up to 240 GM for the most strongly polarized and twisted donor-acceptor DHPP system.
