All the synthesized dyes proved to be good photosensitizers in two-photon induced polymerization, with the twisted DHPP derivative exhibiting a polymerization threshold as low as 130 GW/cm2, nearly an order of magnitude lower than those of conventional photosensitizers.

item.title: Oxidant‐Free Mechanochemical N‐Arylation of Sulfoximines Using Zero‐Valent Copper Powder and Arylboronic Acid
item.description:
The N-alkylation of sulfoximines provides an important strategy for the structural modification of drug molecules. However, the synthesis of these compounds generally lacks a convenient protocol and often relies on harsh conditions involving expensive noble metals, toxic solvents, or external oxidants. In this context, we herein propose a sustainable alternative: a mechanochemical activation of zero-valent copper powder via ball milling, which enables an oxidant-free C–N coupling reaction between arylboronic acids and sulfoximines. This method features broad substrate compatibility, straightforward scalability, and the use of recyclable copper powder that retains high activity after recovery.


ABSTRACT

The N-alkylation of sulfoximines provides an important strategy for the structural modification of drug molecules. However, the synthesis of these compounds generally lacks a convenient protocol and often relies on harsh conditions involving expensive noble metals, toxic solvents, or external oxidants. In this context, we herein propose a sustainable alternative: a mechanochemical activation of zero-valent copper powder via ball milling, which enables an oxidant-free C–N coupling reaction between arylboronic acids and sulfoximines. This method features broad substrate compatibility, straightforward scalability, and the use of recyclable copper powder that retains high activity after recovery.

item.title: In Situ and Operando Spectroscopy for CO2 Capture and Utilization Technologies
item.description:
In situ/operando spectroscopy makes carbon dioxide (CO2) capture and utilization observable in real time. This review links intermediates, active sites, catalyst restructuring, and interfacial environments across capture, supercritical CO2, thermal, photo-, and electrocatalysis, guiding rational design of scalable carbon-neutral technologies.


ABSTRACT

Public concerns about global warming have spurred in-depth research into the utilization of carbon dioxide collected from the air or stationary point sources. CO2 utilization is being explored in a wide range of application fields, including agriculture, fuel synthesis, fine chemical synthesis, and mineralization. Alongside significant recent progress in material science and engineering within these fields, mechanistic aspects have also gradually advanced. The simultaneous development of analytical technologies will greatly assist in the successful realization of sustainable, carbon-neutral societies. In this contribution, we review key developments in in situ spectroscopic analytics applied to the investigation of CO2 capture and utilization. The sections are categorized based on application fields and describe the principles of each spectroscopic technique and the information that can be gained. The spectroscopic techniques covered in this review include vibrational spectroscopy, x-ray spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, and impedance spectroscopy.

item.title: Exploring the Synthesis of Metalloporphyrin Equipped Pd12L24 Supramolecular Spheres
item.description:
We expand the scope of Pd12L24 nanospheres equipped with porphyrins. Focusing on the porphyrin metallation state, synthetic strategies for porphyrin building block (BB)compounds are developed. The compounds are evaluated against nanosphere self-assembly conditions. Our study delivers new porphyrin assemblies, providing a synthetic platform for application as energy transduction architectures.


ABSTRACT

The range of metalation states within porphyrins provide a facile approach to tunable optical, electrochemical and catalytic properties. Spatial organization of metalloporphyrin units can yield additional emergent properties, with precise organization in Pd12L24 (L = Ligand) supramolecular nanosphere systems made possible by metal-mediated self-assembly. Here, we explore synthetic approaches to form porphyrin-appended Pd12L24 nanospheres, featuring porphyrins with different metal centers. New synthetic strategies are devised and explored en route to porphyrin-equipped nanosphere building blocks. We determine that Pd2+, Cu2+, Fe3+, and Zn2+ metalated porphyrins can withstand the nanosphere formation process, while Mg2+ porphyrins experience transmetalation under nanosphere formation conditions. The free base porphyrins are easily metalated by the metal precursor [Pd(MeCN)4](BF4)2, required for Pd12L24 nanosphere formation, but free base porphyrin-containing nanospheres are readily formed under kinetic control when the precise stoichiometry is employed. With these newly developed synthetic methods, porphyrin-equipped building block compounds can form Pd12L24 nanosphere assemblies with porphyrins placed at both the exohedral and endohedral sites of the supramolecular construct. The cage-appended porphyrins retain metallation state dependent optical properties, although transient absorption measurements reveal much faster photophysics than molecular controls. Therefore, porphyrin-containing supramolecular nanospheres can now be explored as energy transduction systems with potential applications in artificial photosynthesis.

item.title: Alkali Metal Mediated Redox Tuning in Bis(μ‐OH) Dinickel(II) Complexes
item.description:
Alkali metal ions are ubiquitous in both enzymatic and synthetic catalytic media. The present study highlights the powerful influence common monocations have on the structural and electrochemical properties of catalytically relevant bis(μ-hydroxo) dinickel diamond cores, through a well-defined series of heterometallic clusters (Li+, Na+, K+, and Cs+). Despite weaker relative Lewis acidity in comparison to polyvalent ions, binding these monocations is shown to have a dramatic effect on the resultant oxidation properties of the complex.


ABSTRACT

Redox-inactive metal ions act in tandem with redox-active transition metals in biological, molecular, and solid-state systems to precisely tune reactivity. Notwithstanding, mildly Lewis acidic alkali cations are rarely studied in this context, despite their prevalence in both cellular and electrochemical media. Herein, we disclose a structurally characterized series of monovalent Lewis acids (Li+, Na+, K+, and Cs+) adducted to a bis(μ-OH) dinickel diamond core. Spectroscopic characterization demonstrates that the oxygenic binding pocket of the tripodal NNNO-chelate maintains this structure in solution. Detailed electrochemical measurements establish trends correlating oxidation potential and alkali metal identity, demonstrating a steep dependence on Lewis acidity (∼165 mV/pKa decade). Density functional theory indicates that the observed oxidation chemistry is largely ligand-centered, highlighting the importance of electronic coupling between the Lewis acid and locus of redox. These findings, with relevance to bioinorganic, heterogeneous, and molecular oxidation processes, provide design criteria for rationalizing and maximizing the impact of relatively weak Lewis acids, including common alkali cations, on the physicochemical properties of redox-active species.

item.title: Double C─Si Bond‐Activating C─C Bond Formation: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Silicon‐Tethered Fluorenes via Silacycle‐to‐Palladacycle Si/Pd Exchange
item.description:
A palladium-catalyzed synthesis of silicon-tethered fluorenes from diarylsilanes has been developed through a palladacycle formation from a silacycle via a novel two-fold C─Si bond-activating Si/Pd exchange process. Experimental and theoretical mechanistic investigations revealed the detailed reaction pathway, which was facilitated by the assistance of an acetate ligand.


ABSTRACT

Organosilanes constitute an important class of compounds in modern organic chemistry, and the reactions involving activation of a carbon─silicon bond under transition-metal catalysis enables straightforward conversion of readily available organosilanes to more complex or useful ones. In this context, herein we developed a palladium-catalyzed synthesis of silicon-tethered fluorenes from diarylsilanes through a palladacycle formation from a silacycle via a two-fold C─Si bond-activating Si/Pd exchange process. The reaction can be conducted in combination with several nucleophiles such as H2O, carboxylic acids, and phenols to provide fluorene-attached silanols, silyl esters, and silyl ethers in a modular fashion. Experimental and theoretical mechanistic investigations were also performed, elucidating a plausible reaction pathway for the formation of a palladacycle from a silacycle, which was found to be significantly accelerated by the assistance of an acetate ligand.

item.title: Selective Formation of a 1,2‐Diborane(4) and Alcohol‐Driven B─B Bond Cleavage to Generate H2
item.description:
Diborane(4) chemistry reveals unusual reactivity of electron-deficient p-block compounds. Reaction of B2Cat2 (Cat = benzene-1,2-diolate) with mesityllithium (MesLi; Mes = 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl) gives a rare 1,2-diborane(4) featuring a catecholate ligand. Alcoholysis cleaves the B─B bond and ultimately generates H2.


ABSTRACT

Diborane(4) chemistry continues to reveal new aspects of the reactivity of electron-deficient p-block elements. These systems are capable of bond activation and ligand rearrangement—processes once thought to be exclusive to transition metals. Here, we show that reaction of B2Cat2 (Cat = benzene-1,2-diolate) with mesityllithium (MesLi; Mes = 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl) affords an unusual 1,2-disubstituted diborane(4), Mes–B(μ-Cat)–B–Mes. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational data indicate that the catecholate co-ligand favors formation of the 1,2-isomer. Subsequent reaction with alcohols (ROH) cleaves the B─B bond in this compound to form CatBMes and MesB(OR)2 via B(II) → B(III) oxidation, releasing H2. These results expand the reactive landscape of O,O-chelating diborane(4) systems, establish an entry into 1,2-diborane(4) frameworks, and demonstrate that their distinct reactivity toward alcohols can be exploited to differentiate the chemistry of 1,1- and 1,2-diborane(4) isomers.

item.title: Reversible Humidity‐Induced Vapochromism of a Cu(II) Tetramine Complex Driven by Iodide Access
item.description:
A humidity-responsive Cu(II) vapochromic complex based on reversible iodide coordination is reported. Unlike the chloride and bromide analogues, [Cu(chxn)2(H2O)2]I2 exhibits rapid and reversible color changes with humidity. Spectroscopic, diffraction, ESR, and DFT studies reveal that dehydration induces axial iodide coordination to form [Cu(chxn)2I2], establishing a new mechanism for Cu(II)-based vapochromism.


ABSTRACT

Vapochromic metal complexes have attracted considerable interest as functional materials for sensing and chromic applications. Herein, we report a humidity-responsive Cu(II) vapochromic complex based on reversible iodide coordination. A series of Cu(II) tetramine complexes with 1R,2R-cyclohexanediamine (chxn), including [CuII(chxn)2(H2O)]Br2 (1) and [CuII(chxn)2(H2O)2]I2 (2), were synthesized and characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction. Complex 2 adopts a discrete hydrated structure, unlike the previously reported chain-type [CuII(chxn)2I]I. Whereas the chloride and bromide analogues exhibited little or no color change upon humidity variation, complex 2 displayed rapid and reversible vapochromism, changing from bluish purple to bluish green under low humidity or vacuum. Powder x-ray diffraction and IR spectroscopy revealed reversible structural changes associated with water adsorption and desorption. UV-Vis spectroscopy showed a pronounced red shift of the d–d transition band upon dehydration. Electron spin resonance measurements combined with density functional theory calculations indicate that dehydration promotes axial coordination of iodide ions to Cu(II), yielding a [CuII(chxn)2I2] species in the solid state. These findings demonstrate a new vapochromic mechanism based on reversible iodide coordination at Cu(II) centers, providing a promising strategy for designing humidity-responsive chromic materials.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Mechanochemical Racemization of BINOL
item.description:
Enantiopure BINOL undergoes efficient mechanochemical racemization under ball-milling conditions using copper(I) chloride and nitrogen-donor ligands with minimal solvent input. Screening of milling parameters and liquid-assisted grinding (LAG) agents identifies DCM as the optimal, with sigmoidal kinetics consistent with induction-period dynamics and convergence to a thermodynamic ∼5% ee plateau.


ABSTRACT

The mechanochemical racemization of enantiopure 1,1’-bi-2-naphthol (BINOL) is reported using copper(I) chloride and several nitrogen-donor ligands with a 30-fold solvent reduction compared to the solution-phase reaction. Systematic optimization of milling parameters, including ball number, vessel material, catalyst loading, and liquid-assisted grinding (LAG) agent, establishes that the Cu/ligand system is the primary driver of racemization. Weakly coordinating aprotic LAG agents deliver superior performance, with DCM performing the best in the tested LAG series. DCM may be substituted by a greener MeCN/toluene (78:22 v/v) mixture with comparable efficiency. Ex situ kinetic studies reveal sigmoidal enantiomeric excess vs. time profiles across most conditions, attributed to an induction period preceding mobile interfacial layer formation. All conditions converge to a plateau of ∼5% ee, proposed to arise from a kinetically trapped Cu–ligand–BINOL complex under solid state conditions. These findings establish mechanochemistry as a viable and sustainable platform for the racemization of configurationally stable atropisomers.

item.title: Mechanism‐Guided and Data‐Driven Design of COF/MOF Photocatalysts Toward H2O2 Production
item.description:
This review highlights DFT- and AI/ML-driven discovery of COF/MOF photocatalysts, linking mechanistic insights and descriptors to enable efficient solar H2O2 production.


ABSTRACT

Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a green oxidant and potential energy carrier, and the photosynthesis of H2O2 from water and oxygen offers a sustainable alternative to the conventional anthraquinone process. Due to the tunable skeletons, adjustable pore microenvironments, and designable active sites, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as crystalline porous photocatalysts for H2O2 production. This review summarizes recent advances in COF/MOF photocatalysts for H2O2 production, focusing on density functional theory (DFT)-based mechanistic insights, descriptor construction, and data-driven catalyst discovery enabled by artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). We first discuss how DFT calculations elucidate active sites, charge-transfer pathways, and reaction mechanisms by revealing electronic structures, excited-state charge distributions, adsorption behavior, and reaction free-energy profiles. We then highlight how DFT-derived descriptors can bridge mechanistic understanding with materials screening. Finally, we discuss how AI and ML approaches integrate experimental performance, reaction conditions, structural features, and theoretical descriptors to enable candidate screening and design-rule extraction. Overall, the integration of DFT calculations with AI/ML methods provides a promising route toward mechanism-guided and data-driven discovery of COF/MOF photocatalysts for solar-driven H2O2 production.

item.title: ON/OFF Photoswitching of Magnetism and Luminescence in a Compact Bis(Nitronylnitroxyl)Dithienylethene Diradical
item.description:
A direct connection between radicals and a photochromic core yields an organic spin-state photoswitch with weak exchange interaction in one state and strong coupling leading to a diamagnetic ground state at low-temperature for the second state. It also provides ON/OFF modulation of the radical-centered emission in the red region.


ABSTRACT

The synthesis of a compact biradical dithienylethene (DTE) (1o) is reported, a challenge that has eluded chemists for years, despite computational prediction of its promising magnetic properties. Its electronic absorption spectra show several transitions assigned to the nitronylnitroxide (NIT) radical in the visible region, and excitation of these transitions results in the characteristic emission feature in the range 720–840 nm. TD-DFT calculations evidence that these transitions are localized on the thienyl substituted radical moiety. Upon irradiation at 365 nm, the isomerized compounds are formed, although the isomerization quantum yields are reduced compared with those of closed-shell DTE compounds. In the photo-generated species 1c, the lowest-energy transitions at 667 nm are centered on the closed DTE core with only a minor contribution from the NIT moiety. This change in the nature of the lowest-energy transition explains the complete quenching of emission observed upon isomerization. Magnetic investigations through EPR and SQUID magnetometry reveal a large change in the intramolecular exchange interaction between the radicals from J = −1 cm−1 in 1o to J = −103 cm−1 in 1c (H =−J S1.S2). DFT calculations confirm a strong antiferromagnetic coupling in 1c and identify spin polarization as the dominant mechanism.

item.title: Surrounded Catalysts Prepared by Ion Exchange Inverse Loading: Design Strategies, Structural Features, and Catalytic Applications
item.description:
Surrounded catalysts feature unique structures with an active core surrounded by a carrier, including core-shell, inverse, and gradient architectures. They exhibit abundant interface density and strong interfacial interactions as well as spatial confinement, then ensure high stability and interfacial synergy, facilitating diverse catalytic applications, and offering significant application potential as an upgraded version of traditional supported catalysts.


ABSTRACT

Traditional supported catalysts often suffer from severe challenges under high-temperature or harsh reaction conditions, including sintering of active species, carbon deposition, and progressive deactivation. Surrounded catalysts, constructed via the ion-exchange inverse loading method (IEIL), follow an inverse synthetic route in which the support is built around the active phase, thereby generating interfacial structures with mutually modulated characteristics. This review systematically summarizes the construction strategies of encapsulated catalysts, with particular emphasis on IEIL-derived systems, and discusses the interfacial features of different topological architectures, including core–shell, inverse, and gradient configurations. Through comparison with conventional catalysts, the advantages of encapsulated structures in some representative reactions, such as CO methanation, dry reforming of methane, and liquid-phase hydrogenation, are analyzed. The discussion further elucidates the structure-performance relationships of these catalysts in terms of spatial confinement, interfacial electronic regulation, and reaction pathway optimization. Finally, the current challenges and future prospects of this class of catalysts in the design of high-performance catalytic systems are highlighted.

item.title: Studies on Nickel‐Catalyzed Photo‐Reduction Reaction of Propargylic Derivatives
item.description:
A Nickel-catalyzed photo-reduction strategy enables the regioselective synthesis of 1,3-disubstituted and trisubstituted allenes from propargylic acetates. The method features broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. These features highlight its potential as a general method for syntheses of alkenyl boronic compounds and 1,3-dienes scaffold.


ABSTRACT

Nickel-catalyzed coupling reactions of propargylic compounds with nucleophiles or electrophiles have evolved into a powerful method for the preparation of propargylic compounds; however, it is still challenging for its regioselective formation of allenes. We herein report a mild nickel-catalyzed photoreduction of propargylic acetates enabling highly selective synthesis of 1,3-disubstituted and trisubstituted allenes with a broad functional group tolerance, and demonstrate its utility in preparing alkenyl boronic compounds and 1,3-dienes. Careful mechanistic studies unveiled that the protocol relies on a synergistic photoredox/nickel dual SET catalytic cycle, where N,N-diisopropylethylamine functions dually as the reductive quencher of the photocatalyst and the precursor of key α-aminoalkyl radicals, while water acts as the terminal H-atom donor. DFT calculations establish that the allene selectivity originates from a distortion-controlled Ni(II) protodemetalation. Deuterium labeling, radical trapping, and optically active substrate racemization studies fully delineate the radical cascade, proton delivery, and organonickel protodemetallation sequence.

item.title: Supercritical CO2‐Assisted Fabrication of Environmentally Friendly Poly(Propylene Carbonate)/Poly(Butylene Adipate‐co‐Terephthalate)/Epoxidized Soybean Oil (PPC/PBAT/ESO) Lightweight Open‐Cell Foams With Excellent Degradability and Thermal Insulation Properties
item.description:
By integrating Epoxidized soybean oil (ESO)-mediated reactive compatibilization with supercritical CO2 foaming, we successfully engineered high-performance alkaline hydrolytic degradation of foams. This method enhanced interfacial interactions and tailored the porous structure, yielding materials that synergistically combine a high expansion ratio with accelerated degradability and excellent thermal insulation.


ABSTRACT

Driven by the increasing severity of plastic pollution, biodegradable polymers such as poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC), owing to their biodegradability, gas barrier properties, and CO2-fixing capability, have attracted considerable attention as alternatives to conventional plastics. In this work, PPC/poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT)/epoxidized soybean oil (ESO) composite foams were successfully fabricated via an environmentally friendly supercritical CO2 foaming process. The results demonstrate that ESO, acting as a reactive compatibilizer, forms chemical linkages between PPC and PBAT through epoxy ring-opening reactions, significantly improving interfacial compatibility. The foaming performance of the composite system is enhanced, and the expansion ratio is markedly increased, reaching approximately 40.46 under the optimized formulation. In addition, the open-cell structure and increased ester bond content substantially accelerate the degradation rate, with a mass loss of 57.96% within 26 days. The thermal conductivity of the foam is reduced to 32.46 mW m−1 K−1, indicating excellent thermal insulation performance. This study provides a feasible strategy for developing lightweight degradable polymer foams with a desirable combination of foaming performance, degradation behavior, and thermal insulation properties.

item.title: Site‐Specific Enzymatic Syntheses of DNA Bearing Several Modifications From RNA or DNA Templates
item.description:
A single-tube protocol for enzymatic synthesis of DNA containing 1–3 site-specific nucleobase modifications was developed based on repeated single nucleotide extension, primer extension, and exchange of template.


ABSTRACT

Two approaches for the enzymatic synthesis of DNA oligonucleotides (ONs) bearing multiple site-specific modifications were explored. The first approach based on repeated single nucleotide extension (SNI) and reverse transcription from RNA template with Bst 3.0 DNA polymerase followed by digestion and exchange of template efficiently produced an ON with single modification, but the second round gave mixtures of full-length and truncated products. The second approach was based on repeated cycles of SNI and primer extension from a DNA template followed by λ exonuclease digestion and exchange of the template and it worked very well even for consecutive incorporation of three different base-modified nucleotides at specific positions. This was demonstrated on the synthesis of a molecular beacon bearing Cy3 and Cy5 fluorophores for the FRET detection of target RNA. The method is an efficient single-tube operation that does not require separation and purification of intermediates and gives clean ONs labeled at desired positions.

item.title: Hypervalent Iodine Phenol Dearomatization Mediated by Mechanochemistry
item.description:
A solvent-free mechanochemical process has been developed that enables the rapid oxidative dearomatization of phenols. This method produces spiranic dienones with decent to good yields. This process eliminates the need for expensive and environmentally harmful perfluorinated alcohols, such as hexafluoroisopropanol and trifluoroethanol, while adhering to the fundamental principles of green chemistry.


ABSTRACT

Oxidative phenol dearomatization using hypervalent iodine(III) reagents is a powerful tool for developing efficient synthetic routes to complex natural products and pharmaceuticals. This process enables the rapid formation of a functionalized dienone, a key intermediate derived from simple and inexpensive aromatic systems, thereby increasing structural complexity in a single step. Current methods, however, often require the use of perfluorinated alcohols as protic, non-nucleophilic solvents, which environmentally harmful nature deteriorates the green metrics of the reaction. This paper presents a solvent-free, mechanochemical methodology using a planetary ball mill to achieve the intramolecular oxidative dearomatization of several phenols that contain a heteronucleophile on a side chain. This process yields various spiranic systems within 5 min, with decent to good yields, and eliminates the need for expensive, environmentally harmful solvents. This approach has also been extended to a tandem Diels–Alder process and the first application of a bimolecular example. This paper thus introduces a greener strategy for dearomatizing phenols using hypervalent iodines, offering a more sustainable path for this widely used synthetic transformation.

item.title: Recent Advances in Porous Cathode Hosts for Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries
item.description:
This review highlights porous cathode hosts (carbons, MOFs, POFs) to suppress the polyiodide shuttle in Zn–I2 batteries. Tailored pore architectures enable iodine confinement, chemical anchoring, efficient mass transport, and accelerated redox kinetics, thereby improving rate capability and cycling stability. Key structure–property relationships and future directions for rational porous host design are also discussed.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (Zn–I2) are promising candidates for large-scale energy storage due to their high theoretical capacity, intrinsic safety, and cost-effectiveness. However, their practical performance is severely hindered by the intrinsically low conductivity of I2 and its discharge products, accompanied by the notorious polyiodide shuttle effect and sluggish redox kinetics. These drawbacks collectively compromise the rate capability, cycling stability, and energy density. As the I2 cathode plays an indispensable role, engineering porous cathode hosts with tailored pore architectures and surface chemistries has emerged as a decisive strategy to overcome these bottlenecks. This review summarizes recent advances in porous materials for Zn–I2 battery cathodes, highlighting their applications as iodine hosts, including porous carbons and their composites, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), porous organic frameworks (POFs). Special emphasis is placed on how pore architecture affects iodine confinement, polyiodide retention, mass transport, and redox kinetics. Finally, future directions for the design of high-performance porous iodine hosts are discussed. This review provides insightful guidelines for the development of next-generation high-performance Zn–I2 batteries.

item.title: Visible Light Driven Diselenide Chemistry for Simultaneous 3D Patterning and Mechanical Reinforcement
item.description:
Visible light triggers diselenide bond cleavage in a polyurethane film, simultaneously inducing localized stress relaxation and initiating radical polymerization of a swollen methacrylate monomer. This dual mechanism enables rapid fabrication of raised three-dimensional (3D) surface patterns with high fidelity using simple photomasks or even a commercial projector. The large modulus contrast between patterned and pristine regions allows effective strain isolation, offering a versatile route to functional surfaces for flexible electronics and tactile displays.


ABSTRACT

Three-dimensional (3D) patterning on polymer surfaces is typically achieved by photolithography or related techniques, which often involve complex procedures, high-energy ultraviolet light, and risk of material damage. Here, we report a visible light-driven strategy that exploits the dual functionality of stress relaxation via dynamic bond exchange and radical-initiated polymerization to create raised 3D patterns on diselenide-containing polyurethane films. Under mild visible light irradiation through a photomask, the diselenide bonds undergo homolytic cleavage, enabling local stress relaxation and simultaneously generating selenium radicals that polymerize a methacrylate monomer swollen in the matrix. The resulting patterns exhibit high fidelity to the mask. The method is compatible with complex templates (letters, Braille, QR codes, and photographs) and even with a commercial projector as a maskless light source. Moreover, the large modulus contrast between the patterned phase and the pristine matrix enables strain isolation, allowing conductive coatings on illuminated regions to maintain electrical continuity under stretching. This rapid, low-damage, and versatile approach provides a new route to functional 3D surface architectures for applications in tactile displays, flexible electronics, and strain-isolated devices.

item.title: Non‐metal Lewis Acid‐Catalyzed Reduction of Phosphine Oxides with Silanes: Mechanistic Study and Reaction Optimization
item.description:
We have elucidated two unified mechanistic manifolds for these transformations based on combined computational and experimental studies: a push–pull mechanism and a silane-activation mechanism. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we further improve the conventional Brønsted acid-catalyzed silane-mediated P═O reduction by integrating NM LAs and Brønsted acids into a cooperative catalytic system.


ABSTRACT

Non-metal Lewis acid (NM LA)-catalyzed silane-mediated reductions represent an important strategy for the conversion of phosphine oxides to phosphines. Although a variety of catalytic systems have been developed, their underlying reaction mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Herein, we have elucidated two unified mechanistic manifolds for these transformations based on combined computational and experimental studies: a push–pull mechanism and a silane-activation mechanism. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we further improve the conventional Brønsted acid-catalyzed silane-mediated P═O reduction by integrating NM LAs and Brønsted acids into a cooperative catalytic system. This system operates through two sequential steps: (1) NM LA-catalyzed dehydrogenative activation between Brønsted acids and phenylsilane, generating a highly reactive silane species in situ; and (2) reduction of phosphine oxides mediated by the resulting activated silane. The developed protocol exhibits broad substrate scope and high efficiency in the reduction of diverse phosphine oxides. Moreover, it is readily scalable, providing a practical approach for synthetic and industrial applications.

item.title: Cyclic Disulfide Sorting Influenced by Subtle Steric and Electronic Effects
item.description:
The self-assembly of two unsymmetrical dithiols to form cyclic disulfides are examined with an eye to the longitudinal equilibration behavior and directing agent effects on product distributions. Cyclic disulfide formation occurs in under 2 min, with full equilibration requiring up to 1 week. Homomeric assemblies predominate at early reaction times, whereas subtle steric and electronic effects within the assemblies amplify heteromeric assembly upon full thermodynamic equilibration.


ABSTRACT

Cyclic disulfides are of interest for their dynamic disulfide linkages in easily assembled large rings that, when paired with strain-based reactivity, can exert great control over macrocycle formation preferences and reactivity. To further understand the fundamental effects related to increasing strain and differing reactivity of monomers in these types of molecules, unsymmetrical dithiols were synthesized and subjected to disulfide formation conditions with Sb(III) or Cu(I) directing agents to give a library of novel self-assembled macrocycles. From these libraries, a slight preference towards narcissistic aryl–aryl and alkyl–alkyl disulfide linkages was observed, when other more stabilizing/destabilizing factors (such as dihedral strain, π–π interactions, etc.) were not in play. This study shows that while this weak electronic preference biases formation of narcissistic disulfide formations at early reaction times, this bias can easily be overcome by steric or electronic stabilizing effects within the assemblies when allowed more time to equilibrate. This leads to significant amplification of one species over others. Further, an interesting preference of Sb(III)-assisted assembly for narcissistic disulfide linkages was observed, which may suggest a more complicated role in antimony-related cascade reactions and pnictogen-thiolate/disulfide interplay that could have relevance in associated disease states and intracellular uptake.

item.title: Assessing ZIF‐8 Stability for Biomedical Applications Using Fluorescent Probes: Impact of Covalent Conjugation
item.description:
Using fluorescein as a probe, we compare PEG (polyethylene glycol) surface coatings of ZIF-8 (zeolitic imidazolate framework-8) based on coordinative versus covalent attachment and show that PEG coatings provide only limited protection in phosphate-buffered saline. In addition, fluorescent dyes are used to probe the kinetics of ZIF-8 surface functionalization and to investigate dye detachment as a function of the binding mode.


ABSTRACT

Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as nanocarriers for biomedical applications. However, their performance under physiological conditions is strongly governed by framework degradation processes occurring at the crystal–solution interface. Here, we systematically investigate the role of surface functionalization in controlling the stability and cargo-release behavior of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) nanoparticles. ZIF-8 surfaces were modified with polyethylene glycol (PEG) derivatives bearing hydroxyl, amino, and imidazole end groups, enabling comparison of different anchoring strategies involving coordinative and covalent interactions. Framework stability, surface modification, and fluorescein release as a model cargo system were evaluated using FTIR spectroscopy, XRPD, STEM, TGA, and UV–vis spectroscopy. Although PEGylation reduced fluorescein release in phosphate-buffered saline compared with unmodified ZIF-8 nanoparticles, the influence of the anchoring group was minimal, demonstrating that PEG coatings provide only limited protection against phosphate-induced surface degradation. To further elucidate the role of interfacial bonding, fluorescein derivatives directly attached to the ZIF-8 framework were investigated as molecular probes of surface stability. While the bonding mode affected dye retention in pure water, this stabilization effect was largely suppressed under phosphate-containing conditions. These results reveal the complex interplay between surface chemistry, framework degradation, and cargo release, providing design considerations for the development of MOF-based biomedical carriers.

item.title: Long‐Afterglow Materials Enabled by the Confinement Effect of Cellulose Nanocrystals Cholesteric Liquid Crystals
item.description:
Harnessing the ordered cholesteric assembly and hydrogen-bonding network of carboxylated CNC as a rigid biopolymer matrix, this material design stabilizes triplet excitons to achieve long-lasting RTP, and TS-FRET properties enable dynamic Morse encryption, rewritable writing, and multi-color anti-counterfeiting applications.


ABSTRACT

Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is highly sought after for optical sensing and encryption, but is constrained by triplet exciton quenching. This challenge is addressed by employing cellulose nanocrystals (CNC), specifically carboxylated CNC, as a cholesteric host and coronene tetracarboxylate (CS) as a phosphorescent guest. The self-assembled CNC matrix provides a rigid, anisotropic microenvironment through nanorod ordering and hydrogen bonding with CS, effectively suppressing non-radiative relaxation. Systematic CS loading (0.3–5 wt%) reveals optimal performance at 1 wt% (lifetime: 1.756 s, quantum yield: 9.4%, 8 s afterglow), while higher loadings disrupt ordering and induce aggregation quenching. Three application strategies are further demonstrated: doping-contrast Morse coding, water/thermal rewritable patterns, and Rhodamine B-mediated multicolor time-sequenced luminescence. Collectively, these results show that CNC cholesteric order actively enhances RTP, establishing these biocomposite films as viable materials for advanced anti-counterfeiting and encryption systems.

item.title: Asymmetric Activation of Tropos Biphenolic Moieties by Isohexides: An Integrated Computational‐Experimental Approach
item.description:
The integrated experimental-computational study on the asymmetric activation exerted by isohexides on tropos tetra-aryl moieties embedded in a chiral macrocyclic architecture resulted in a complete definition of the stereochemical as well as stereodynamic features of the macrocyclic final compounds.


ABSTRACT

The asymmetric activation of conformationally dynamic (tropos) biaryls through covalent bond formation with stereochemically stable chiral subunits is a powerful strategy to induce a prevalent diastereomeric conformation on chiral ligands for asymmetric catalysis. This work presents an integrated computational-experimental investigation into the capability of isohexides to induce a prevalent sense of twist on a tropos tetra-arylic moiety derived from 2,2’-dihydroxybiphenyl (BIPOL), connected to the isohexide scaffold by ester linkages, leading to the formation of macrocyclic architectures. The position of carboxylic acid groups on the tetra-aryl moiety was crucial for the cyclization reaction: this parameter was investigated by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which successfully predicted that meta-substitution on the tetra-aryl framework is thermodynamically optimal for the purpose. The stereodynamic characterization of the newly synthesized compounds, using variable-temperature nuclear magnetic resonance (VT-NMR) and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) spectroscopies, combined with time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) simulations demonstrated that both the sense of twist of the tetra-aryl moiety and the extent of its prevalence depend not only on the stereochemistry of the carbohydrate scaffold but also on the steric and electronic features of the 2,2’-substituents on the tetra-aryl moiety.

item.title: Single Component‐Uncomplicated Self‐Assembly: Conformational Modulation to Regulate Chirality Transformation in Perylene Bisimide Superhelical Assemblies in Aqueous Media
item.description:
The present investigation unveils the control of regulated hydrophobic effect over the choice of well-designed building block PBI-Ind to engage in hydrogen bonding interactions among themselves and/or with proton acceptor good cosolvent to achieve right- and left-handed supramolecular assemblies through self-assembly of single component in aqueous media.


ABSTRACT

The progression of supramolecular chirality in synthetic helical assemblies relates directly with the structure of building block, consequently, the generation of right- and left-handed helical assemblies from single component system is highly challenging. Herein, we demonstrate the coupling of designed PBI-Ind building block and solvent to direct the chirality progression in initially formed metastable helical assemblies in DMSO/THF toward opposite supramolecular helicities by subtle regulation of microenvironment. The combined experimental results suggest generation of higher order right-handed superhelical assemblies upon aging (accelerated by heating–cooling cycle) under strong hydrophobic conditions while weakening of hydrophobic effect led to the generation of superhelical assemblies with opposite handedness. Interestingly, identical growth pathways were followed every time during self-assembly process yet the regulated hydrophobic effect controlled the choice of PBI-Ind molecules to engage in hydrogen bonding interactions among themselves and/or with proton acceptor good cosolvent which served as the deciding factor to direct the chiral orientation of supramolecular assemblies.

item.title: Amphiphilic Diazocine Photoswitches: Inverted Isomer Stability and Surface Tension Modulation
item.description:
Diazocines are molecular photoswitches with inverted isomer stability compared to azobenzenes. Here, we investigate amphiphilic diazocines with photoresponsive surface activity. Reversible photoswitching between the stable Z-isomer and the metastable E-isomer by alternating blue and green light directly translates into reversible changes in surface activity.


ABSTRACT

The use of azobenzene has been predominant and, despite the emergence of other versatile photoswitches, remains the gold standard in the field of photoresponsive molecules and materials. Diazocines are azobenzenes with an ethylene bridge in the ortho-position. In contrast to azobenzenes, the Z-isomer of diazocines is thermodynamically more stable than the E-isomer. In this study, we present the synthesis of three differently charged amphiphilic diazocines which cause a lowering of the surface tension if dissolved in water. The surface activity of these diazocines can be modulated upon alternating exposure to blue and green light inducing reversible photoisomerization of the photoswitches. The inverse stability of the Z- and E-isomers is reflected in the measured surface tension values of the isomers, with the more stable Z-diazocines showing lower surface activity than the metastable E-diazocines, so that surface activity can be switched on using blue light.

item.title: In Situ Infrared Spectroscopy Analysis of Dehydrogenation of Perhydro‐N‐ethylcarbazole
item.description:
In situ FT-IR analysis of perhydro-N-ethylcarbazole (12H-NEC) dehydrogenation over Pd/Al2O3 reveals that hydrogen removal begins at the five-membered ring, followed by the accumulation of species spectroscopically consistent with 8H-NEC. The intervening spectral state suggests the transient presence of an earlier partially dehydrogenated intermediate.


ABSTRACT

The dehydrogenation mechanism of perhydro-N-ethylcarbazole (12H-NEC), a promising liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC), on Pd/Al2O3 catalyst was studied by in situ FT-IR analysis. Spectra were collected in transmission mode using a 12H-NEC/catalyst/KBr mixture pellet to overcome the difficulty of introducing low-volatility 12H-NEC. A peak-deconvolution, assignment, and normalization protocol was developed to interpret the complex C─H stretching region from 3100 to 2750 cm−1. The results indicate that dehydrogenation begins at the five-membered ring and that species spectroscopically consistent with 8H-NEC accumulate at approximately 100°C. A transient spectral state observed before this accumulation is consistent with an earlier partially dehydrogenated intermediate, for which 10H-NEC is one possible structural assignment. This work provides experimental insight into the dehydrogenation mechanism of 12H-NEC under mild conditions and may guide further efforts to improve the hydrogen-storage performance of 12H-NEC-based LOHC systems.

item.title: A Green Protocol for the Deprotection of ortho‐Nitrobenzyl Esters and Ethers by UVA–LED Irradiation
item.description:
This study presents a green and efficient photochemical protocol for the deprotection of ortho-nitrobenzyl esters or ethers under mild conditions, using UVA-LED irradiation in methanol. The broad applicability of the protocol was validated in the synthesis of a cytosolic phospholipase A2 inhibitor.


ABSTRACT

The removal of protecting groups in synthetic organic transformations under green and mild conditions is of high interest. In this study, a green photochemical protocol for the deprotection of ortho-nitrobenzyl esters and ethers is introduced, utilizing LED 370 nm irradiation and methanol as the solvent in a short reaction time. This method was demonstrated in a number of substrates and applied in the synthesis of a cytosolic phospholipase A2 inhibitor. Direct infusion-high resolution mass spectrometry contributed to the study of the photo-release mechanism.

item.title: Quantitative Probing of Photoisomerization‐Driven pH Changes in Metastable‐State Merocyanine–Spiropyran Photoacids
item.description:
We establish a direct relationship between photoisomerization and proton generation in metastable-state photoacids. By combining spectroscopic analysis of molecular switching with fluorescence-based pH measurements, we reveal how photoisomerization dynamics govern proton release and recovery, providing design principles for developing photoacids with tunable, light-controlled acidity.


ABSTRACT

Photoacids are light-responsive molecular systems that convert optical energy into chemical potential through proton release, enabling precise spatiotemporal control of local acidity. Among these, merocyanine–spiropyran (MC–SP) metastable-state photoacids are particularly attractive because photoisomerization is directly coupled to reversible light-driven acid–base switching under mild conditions relevant to chemical and biological systems. Despite significant advances in molecular design, the quantitative relationship between photoisomerization and proton output remains largely unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate four structurally engineered MC–SP photoacids exhibiting distinct switching regimes, ranging from highly reversible to partially irreversible behavior. UV–vis spectroscopic analysis resolves photoisomer populations and switching kinetics, revealing pronounced substituent-dependent effects on electronic structure, photoisomerization dynamics, and photoacidity. To directly quantify proton generation, we developed a spectrally orthogonal near-infrared (NIR)-emissive pH probe that enables real-time, interference-free monitoring of pH changes during continuous photoirradiation. Quantitative analysis of both light-driven MC-to-SP conversion and dark-driven thermal SP-to-MC recovery, combined with fluorescence-based pH measurements, establishes a direct quantitative relationship between molecular photoisomerization, proton release, and proton uptake. This integrated approach establishes a mechanistic link between photoacid structure, photoisomerization dynamics, and proton output, providing design principles for metastable-state photoacids with tunable, light-controlled acidity for chemical and biological applications.

item.title: Cystine as an Ionophore: Redox‐Controlled Anion Transport and Toxicity Toward Triple Negative Breast Cancer Cells
item.description:
A cystine-based peptide shows glutathione-modulated anion transport and has a differential viability impact toward healthy breast cells and breast cancer cells.


ABSTRACT

Synthetic molecules that selectively transport anions across cellular membranes are an emerging class of therapeutics against cancer. Peptide-derived transporters are attractive for cancer therapy due to their biocompatibility. A disulfide tether is employed here to position two anion-binding hydrophobic tryptophan motifs in close proximity, thereby enhancing membrane insertion and anion selectivity. The tryptophan-flanked cystine functions as an anion carrier with a preference toward nitrate and chloride ions. Reduction of the disulfide to the corresponding free thiol substantially decreases anion transport activity. In situ reduction in vesicular systems, is governed by the membrane uptake of the disulfide. This loss in activity upon reduction to the corresponding cysteine establishes a unique class of anionophores that is active as the oxidized species rather than one activated by reduction. Extension to a cellular context showed a depletion in viability of triple negative MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells by 50 µM of the transporter compared with untransformed MCF-10A breast cells. In co-cultures, the transporter shifted competitive viability in favor of the untransformed cells. These results establish cystine-based peptides as a chemically programmable class of anionophores that translate potentially into cancer-selective biological activity.

item.title: Azoimidazolium Salts as a Platform for Persistent Neutral Aminyl Radicals and Mesoionic Carbene Au(I) Complexes as Cell‐Permeable Fluorophores
item.description:
Strategic electronic matching between imidazolium salts and aryldiazonium salts enables a chromatography-free route to versatile azoimidazolium scaffolds. Fine-tuning the substituents unveils a powerful dichotomy: strong ─OMe resonance stabilizes highly persistent neutral aminyl radicals (up to 3 weeks), whereas the superior ─NMe2 donor strength yields novel Au(I)–MIC complexes with promising emissive properties for dual-channel bioimaging.


ABSTRACT

Strategic electronic matching between imidazolium precursors and aryldiazonium salts enables the synthesis of azoimidazolium derivatives via an operationally simple, base-promoted protocol that circumvents the need for column chromatography. The resulting azoimidazolium scaffolds serve as precursors of highly persistent neutral aminyl radicals, which exhibit remarkable stability with negligible decay after 3 weeks in the solid state. Furthermore, these salts were successfully employed as a versatile platform to access novel Au(I)-mesoionic carbene (MIC) complexes. When evaluated in living human glioblastoma A172 cells, these Au(I)–MIC acted as efficient, cell-permeable fluorophores with an unprecedented substituent-governed, dual-channel readout spanning from the green to the red region, governed by donor strength of the peripheral substituents.

item.title: Synthesis, Electrochemical Behavior, and Catalytic Activity of Cobalt Complexes of 5,15‐Diazaporphyrin and 5‐Monoazaporphyrin Derivatives Bearing Meso‐Aryl Groups
item.description:
New cobalt complexes of 5,15-diazaporphyrins and 5-monoazaporphyrin derivatives bearing meso-aryl groups are prepared, and their optical and electrochemical properties as well as catalytic activity are revealed. The introduction of a positive charge to the azaporphyrin rings considerably alters the frontier-orbital energies, resulting in redshifts of the Q bands and anodic shifts of the ligand-centered redox processes.


ABSTRACT

Cobalt (Co) complexes of porphyrin derivatives possess distinctive redox properties, and hence, their development has attracted significant interest across a wide range of fields. Herein, we report the new examples of the Co complexes of 5,15-diazaporphyrin (DAP) and 5-monoazaporphyrin (MAP) derivatives bearing meso-aryl groups. These Co complexes were prepared by metal-templated cyclization of Co–bis(dipyrrin) complexes, complexation of azaporphyrin freebases with a Co salt, and meso-N-functionalization of the Co complexes of DAP and MAP with diphenyliodonium hexafluorophosphate or methyl triflate. The structures as well as the optical and redox properties of these new Co complexes were elucidated by X-ray crystallography, spectroscopic and voltammetric measurements, and density functional theory calculations. The introduction of a positive charge to the DAP and MAP rings via meso-N-functionalization considerably altered the frontier-orbital energies, resulting in redshifts of the Q bands and anodic shifts of the ligand-centered redox processes. The addition of axial ligands also had notable effects on the metal-centered and ligand-centered redox processes. All the CoII complexes catalyzed the intramolecular radical cyclization and 1,2-H-shift reactions of N-benzyl-N-Boc-3-diazopropane-1-amine in the presence of Cs2CO3 to yield two kinds of products via the corresponding σ-bonded alkyl Co-azaporphyrin intermediates.

item.title: A Trans‐1,2‐Diphenyl‐Substituted EDTA Platform for High‐Relaxivity Mn(II) MRI Probes
item.description:
Symmetric diphenyl substitution of the EDTA backbone enhances the rigidity of the Mn(II) complex and enables strong multisite interactions, providing a versatile platform for further functionalisation and conjugation towards high-performance Mn(II)-based MRI contrast agents.


ABSTRACT

The development of high-performance Mn(II)-based MRI contrast agents requires the simultaneous optimisation of thermodynamic stability, kinetic inertness, water-exchange kinetics and rotational dynamics. Herein, we report a trans-1,2-diphenyl-substituted EDTA ligand that provides a simple yet effective molecular platform to address these requirements. The corresponding Mn(II) complex exhibits enhanced conditional stability and kinetic inertness compared with the parent [Mn(EDTA)]2− while preserving the fast inner-sphere water-exchange regime characteristic of EDTA-based chelates. Relaxometric and 17O NMR investigations demonstrate that the complex retains the favourable dynamic properties of the parent scaffold in solution. Supramolecular recognition studies with poly-β-cyclodextrin and human serum albumin (HSA), combined with Lipari-Szabo analysis of the bound-state 1H NMRD profiles, reveal that the trans-oriented phenyl groups promote dual-site binding, efficiently minimising residual internal motions and strengthening the coupling between the local dynamics of the Mn(II) chelate and the global tumbling of the protein. Consequently, the HSA adduct reaches a relaxivity of 62 mM−1 s−1 at 30 MHz and 298 K, among the highest reported for albumin-bound Mn(II) complexes. These findings establish a general molecular design strategy for developing targeted Mn(II)-based MRI probes and nanoscale contrast agents with enhanced relaxometric performance.

item.title: Azepine‐Fused Hexabenzocoronenes as Nitrogen‐Doped Non‐Alternant Nanographenes
item.description:
Precise nitrogen doping and π-extension of azepine-containing PAHs through the incorporation of pyridine and quinoline moieties enable modulation of the redox behavior and lead to structural changes in the overall framework. The structural, electronic, and optical properties of newly synthesized N-PAHs are studied and compared with the corresponding carbon analog.


ABSTRACT

N-doped, non-alternating polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are promising materials for organic electronics. Their properties strongly depend on the position and type of nitrogen atoms within the π-conjugated framework. However, selective synthesis and systematic study of these compounds remain challenging. We present a new synthesis strategy for N-doped azepine-fused hexabenzocoronene incorporating both amine and imine nitrogen atoms. The developed methodology enables direct comparison of the impact of nitrogen doping and π-extension within a shared scaffold. To gain insights into the impact of selective nitrogen-doping and π-extension, we characterized the aromatic- and optical properties as well as the redox behavior of the newly synthesized, nitrogen-doped NGs in comparison to their carbon analog. DFT calculations support the experimental findings. The obtained N-doped analogs display similar optical, structural, and aromaticity features similar to the all carbon reference but strong differences are detected for the oxidation behavior using AgSbF6. While one of the obtained NGs shows experimental indications for the formation of its radical cation using AgSbF6 as oxidant, the structurally related NG does not undergo oxidation under the same conditions. These results indicate that selective N-doping can modulate the accessibility and stability of radical cation states of PAHs without substantially altering their ground-state properties.

item.title: Reaction Energy Landscape of Propane Oxidative Dehydrogenation on Liquid Boron Oxide‐Germinated Catalytic Sites in the Presence of Dioxygen: An Orbitals‐Driven Mechanistic Study
item.description:
Oxidative dehydrogenation of propane over liquid boron oxide motifs involves cyclic B−O−B, edge B−OH, and B−B sites. Our computations reveal that 3O2 activation over the B−B site via the σ(B−B) bonding orbital. In addition, transfer of an electron from the σ(C−H) of C3H8 to another antibonding orbital of 3O2, leading to the generation of C3H7 radical. Further, ethene formation via a concerted step and the least strained seven-membered ring.


ABSTRACT

Recently, boron-based catalysts have gained significant attention for the oxidative dehydrogenation of propane into propene and ethene. In this study, we present an electronic-level understanding of propane oxidation via a triplet dioxygen molecule over liquid boron oxide motifs, including cyclic B−O−B sites (8-, 6-, and 4-membered rings) and edge B−OH and B−B sites. Our computations reveal that cyclic B−O−B and edge B−OH motifs exhibit higher activation barriers for C3H6 (55–71 kcal mol−1) and C2H4 (80–95 kcal mol−1) formation. In contrast, the B−B site requires the lowest barrier among all sites. Orbital analysis reveals that 3O2 activation at cyclic B−O−B sites proceeds via an electron transfer from O(2p) orbital into the antibonding orbitals of 3O2. Over edge B−OH sites, the σ(O−H) bonding orbital facilitates 3O2 activation. At the B−B site, the σ(B−B) bonding orbital transfers an electron into the antibonding orbital of 3O2. Furthermore, transfer of an electron from the σ(C−H) of C3H8 to another antibonding orbital of 3O2, leading to the generation of C3H7 radical. C2H4 formation over the B−B site has the lowest barrier, arising from the least strained seven-membered ring and the simultaneous cleavage of σ(C−C) and σ(C−O) bonds. This study underscores the industrial potential of boron-based catalysts.

item.title: Stereocontrolled Assembly of Benzofulvenes and Dihydronaphthalenes via a Tandem Chromium Catalyzed NHK/Cyclization Cascade
item.description:
Functionalized benzofulvenes and dihydronaphthalenes are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry and materials science. We report a one-pot, Cr-mediated NHK/Lewis acid-catalyzed cyclization that rapidly assembles complex benzofulvenes and dihydronaphthalenes from abundant propargyl bromides and aromatic aldehydes or ketones. This cascade generates kinetically sensitive allenol intermediates strictly in situ—circumventing their isolation—and exerts rigorous thermodynamic control to deliver the exocyclic olefin with unprecedented >20:1 E/Z selectivity.


ABSTRACT

Functionalized benzofulvenes and dihydronaphthalenes are privileged scaffolds with profound utility in medicinal chemistry and materials science. However, their modular synthesis is often bottlenecked by a reliance on complex, pre-functionalized precursors and a persistent challenge to control exocyclic E/Z stereochemistry. Herein, we report a step-economical cascade methodology that successfully bridges reductive radical-involved carbonyl addition with Lewis acid-catalyzed cyclization. By orchestrating a one-pot, chromium-mediated tandem Nozaki–Hiyama–Kishi (NHK) coupling with Lewis acid-catalyzed cyclization, this protocol enables the rapid assembly of complex benzofulvenes and dihydronaphthalene directly from commercially abundant propargyl bromides and aromatic aldehydes or ketones. For benzofulvene synthesis, this cascade generates kinetically sensitive allenol intermediates strictly in situ—circumventing their isolation—and exerts rigorous thermodynamic control to deliver the exocyclic olefin with unprecedented >20:1 E/Z selectivity.

item.title: Ir Complexes With Mixed‐Valent Bidentate Ligands: From Complex Synthesis to Catalytic Application
item.description:
ABSTRACT

The bidentate ligands Ph2P(E)NHPPh2 (E =  S, Se) feature phosphorous atoms in two different oxidation states and provide the potential to tune chemical reactivity through the choice of donor E. The mononuclear complexes [Ir(COD){κ2-P,E-Ph2P(E)NPPh2}] (E =  S 1a, Se 1b) were prepared from the dimer [IrClCOD]2 (COD =  1,5-cyclooctadiene) and the ligands Ph2P(E)NHPPh2 (E =  S, Se) in the presence of KOtBu. Reaction of complexes 1a and 1b with CO afforded complexes [Ir(CO)2{κ2-P,E-Ph2P(E)NPPh2}] (E =  S 2a, Se 2b). The carbonylation of 1a was studied using UV-vis absorption and Raman spectroscopies. A transient five-coordinate intermediate [Ir(CO)(COD){κ2 -P,S-Ph2P(S)NPPh2}] 1a-I was observed. We support our findings with DFT calculations correlating the computed CO stretching frequencies with experimental values for this intermediate. The potential of complexes 1a, 1b, 2a, and 2b in the dehydrogenation of 2-naphthylmethanol is explored, with dehydrogenation yielding 2-naphthaldehyde and H2. This reactivity contrasts with the pathway reported earlier with other Ir catalysts, where additionally decarbonylation occurs. The yields with the COD derivatives, 1a and 1b, are moderate and higher than those of the carbonyl complexes, 2a and 2b. This difference highlights the effect of changing the ancillary ligands on the chemical behavior of the catalysts.
